b: Because liquid impurities soak into the leather and there is no solid substance to remove them by friction.

f: 526. Does a cloth garment become purified by rubbing after impurity dries on it?
b: No, it requires washing even after drying.

f: 527. Why must clothing be washed rather than rubbed to remove impurity?
b: Because fabric absorbs impurity deeply and rubbing does not remove all of it.

f: 528. What is the ruling of semen (manī) on clothing according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: If it is wet, it must be washed; if it dries, rubbing it off is sufficient.

f: 529. What evidence is used for the distinction between wet and dry semen?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها: “Wash it if it is wet, and rub it if it is dry.”

f: 530. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s position regarding semen?
b: He considers semen pure.

f: 531. What evidence is used against the view that semen is pure?
b: The report that the Prophet ﷺ instructed washing clothing from semen.

f: 532. What additional narration indicates semen is impure?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said that clothing is washed due to five things, including semen.

f: 533. How is dried semen on clothing purified according to some Ḥanafī scholars?
b: It is purified by scraping (fark), because hardship and widespread difficulty occur with semen on clothing.

f: 534. What was the other narration from Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله regarding dried semen on clothing?
b: Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله held that dried semen is not purified except by washing.

f: 535. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله require washing instead of scraping for dried semen?
b: Because the heat of the body draws the semen back into the garment, and the body itself cannot be purified by scraping.

f: 536. If impurity falls on a mirror or sword, how are they purified?
b: They are purified by wiping them.

f: 537. Why is wiping sufficient to purify a mirror or sword from impurity?
b: Because impurity does not penetrate them, so removing what is on their surface is sufficient.

f: 538. If impurity falls on the ground and dries through sunlight until its traces disappear, is prayer valid on that ground?
b: Yes, prayer is valid on that place according to the Ḥanafī school.

f: 539. What is the opinion of Zufar and al-Shāfiʿī regarding ground purified by sunlight?
b: They do not consider it purified because no physical means of removing the impurity occurred.

f: 540. What evidence do the Ḥanafīs use for the purification of earth by drying?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The purification of the earth is its drying.”

f: 541. Why is tayammum not allowed on ground purified only by sunlight?
b: Because purification of the earth used for tayammum is established by Qurʾānic text, so the prophetic report about drying does not establish its suitability for tayammum.

f: 542. What amount of heavy impurity is excused according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: The amount of a dirham or less.

f: 543. What examples of heavy impurity are mentioned in the text?
b: Blood, urine, wine, chicken droppings, and donkey urine.

f: 544. Is prayer valid if a person has more than a dirham amount of heavy impurity on their body or clothing?
b: No, prayer is not valid.

f: 545. What is the opinion of Zufar and al-Shāfiʿī regarding small amounts of impurity?
b: They hold that any amount of impurity, small or large, prevents valid prayer.

f: 546. Why do the Ḥanafīs excuse a small amount of impurity during prayer?
b: Because completely avoiding small amounts is difficult, so they are overlooked to prevent hardship.

f: 547. How is the amount of a dirham measured according to one narration?
b: It is measured by area, approximately the width of the palm.

f: 548. How is the amount of a dirham measured according to another narration?
b: It is measured by weight, approximately one mithqāl (a large dirham).

f: 549. How are the two measurements of a dirham reconciled?
b: The area measurement applies to thin impurities, while the weight measurement applies to thick impurities.

f: 550. Why are blood, urine, wine, chicken droppings, and donkey urine classified as heavy impurities?
b: Because their impurity is established through decisive evidence.

f: 551. What amount of light impurity is excused according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Up to one quarter of the garment.

f: 552. What example of light impurity is mentioned in the text?
b: The urine of animals whose meat is permissible to eat.

f: 553. Why is the urine of edible animals considered a light impurity according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: Because there is disagreement about its impurity or conflicting evidences regarding it.

f: 554. What are the different explanations for the quarter measurement of light impurity?
b: It may mean one quarter of the smallest garment valid for prayer, or one quarter of the area where the impurity fell, such as the hem.

f: 555. What measurement did Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله give for light impurity?
b: A span by a span.

f: 556. If cow dung exceeds the amount of a dirham on clothing, is prayer valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, prayer is not valid.

f: 557. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله consider cow dung a heavy impurity?
b: Because the evidence declaring it impure is not opposed by another evidence.

f: 558. What is the ruling of cow dung exceeding a dirham according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: Prayer remains valid until the amount becomes excessive.

f: 559. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad consider cow dung a lighter impurity?
b: Because there is room for scholarly disagreement and widespread hardship due to roads being filled with it.

f: 560. Why is cow dung treated differently from donkey urine regarding hardship?
b: Because cow dung commonly fills roads and is difficult to avoid, while donkey urine is absorbed by the earth and is easier to avoid.

f: 561. What was Muḥammad’s later opinion after seeing widespread hardship in Rayy regarding cow dung?
b: He ruled that even a very large amount does not prevent prayer.

f: 562. If horse urine touches clothing, when does it prevent prayer according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: It does not prevent prayer unless it becomes excessive.

f: 563. What is Muḥammad’s opinion regarding horse urine on clothing?
b: It does not prevent prayer even if it becomes excessive.

f: 564. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله treat horse urine as a light impurity?
b: Because horses are considered animals whose meat is eaten by them, or because of conflicting evidence about its impurity.

f: 565. If droppings from birds whose meat is not eaten exceed a dirham amount, is prayer valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: Yes, prayer remains valid.

f: 566. What is Muḥammad’s opinion regarding droppings of birds whose meat is not eaten?
b: Prayer is not valid if they exceed a dirham amount.

f: 567. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله excuse large amounts of non-edible bird droppings?
b: Because birds release them from the air and avoiding them completely is difficult.

f: 568. Why does Muḥammad not excuse non-edible bird droppings?
b: Because there is no necessity since people do not normally mix with them.

f: 569. If droppings from non-edible birds fall into a container, does the water become impure?
b: There are two opinions: some scholars say it becomes impure, while others excuse it due to difficulty avoiding it.

f: 570. If fish blood exceeds a dirham amount, is prayer valid according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes, prayer remains valid.

f: 571. Why is fish blood not considered impure according to the preferred view?
b: Because it is not considered true blood.

f: 572. What was Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله opinion regarding fish blood?
b: He considered a large amount of fish blood impure.

f: 573. If mule or donkey saliva exceeds a dirham amount, is prayer valid?
b: Yes, prayer remains valid.

f: 574. Why does mule or donkey saliva not invalidate prayer according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because its impurity is doubtful, and doubtful impurity does not remove certainty of purity.

f: 575. If tiny drops of urine like the heads of needles splash onto clothing, what is the ruling?
b: They are overlooked because avoiding them is impossible.

f: 576. What are the two categories of physical impurity in Islamic law?
b: Visible impurity (najāsah marʾiyyah) and invisible impurity (najāsah ghayr marʾiyyah).

f: 577. How is visible impurity purified?
b: By removing the actual substance of the impurity.

f: 578. If the substance of visible impurity disappears but a difficult-to-remove trace remains, what is the ruling?
b: The remaining trace is excused.

f: 579. Is repeated washing required after the substance of visible impurity disappears?
b: No, removing the substance itself is sufficient according to this indication.

f: 580. How is invisible impurity purified?
b: By washing until the person washing believes it has been removed.

f: 581. Why is strong probability enough to establish purification from invisible impurity?
b: Because the impurity cannot be directly observed, so certainty is impossible; strong probability is treated like certainty in similar matters.

f: 582. Why did scholars estimate washing invisible impurity three times?
b: Because strong probability of purification is normally achieved after three washes.

f: 583. Is squeezing required when washing impure clothing according to the apparent Ḥanafī narration?
b: Yes, squeezing is required each time because it extracts the impurity.

f: 584. What is the ruling of istinjāʾ (cleaning after relieving oneself) according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: Istinjāʾ is a sunnah because the Prophet ﷺ consistently practiced it.

f: 585. Why is istinjāʾ considered a sunnah rather than obligatory according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because it is established through the Prophet’s ﷺ regular practice rather than an obligatory command.

f: 586. What materials may be used for istinjāʾ besides water?
b: Stones and anything that serves the same purpose may be used.

f: 587. What is the purpose of using stones or similar materials for istinjāʾ?
b: The purpose is achieving cleanliness (inqāʾ), so whatever achieves that purpose is considered.

f: 588. Is there a specific number of stones required for istinjāʾ according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No specific sunnah number is required; the required amount is whatever achieves cleanliness.

f: 589. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding the number of stones required for istinjāʾ?
b: He holds that three stones are required based on the hadith: “Let him perform istinjāʾ with three stones.”

f: 590. What evidence do the Ḥanafīs use to show that three stones are not required?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever uses stones should use an odd number; whoever does so has done well, and whoever does not, there is no harm.”

f: 591. Why do the Ḥanafīs argue that one stone may be sufficient for istinjāʾ?
b: Because an odd number includes one, and a stone with three sides can be used by agreement.

f: 592. Is washing with water after relieving oneself better than using stones?
b: Yes, washing with water is better.

f: 593. What evidence is mentioned for the superiority of washing with water?
b: The verse regarding the people of Qubāʾ: “In it are men who love to purify themselves” (Qurʾān 9:108).

f: 594. Why was the verse about purification revealed according to the text?
b: It was revealed concerning people who used stones and then followed them with water.

f: 595. How much water should be used for istinjāʾ?
b: Water should be used until a person strongly believes that purification has been achieved.

f: 596. Is there a fixed number of washes required when using water for istinjāʾ?
b: No, it is not fixed by number.

f: 597. When is a specific number used for someone performing istinjāʾ?
b: A specific number may be given to someone suffering from excessive doubts (waswasah).

f: 598. How many times is someone with excessive doubts advised to wash according to one opinion?
b: Three times.

f: 599. What other number was mentioned for a person with excessive doubts?
b: Seven times was also mentioned.

f: 600. If impurity spreads beyond its normal exit area, can stones still be used for istinjāʾ?
b: No, water (or according to another narration, any purifying liquid) must be used.

f: 601. Why can stones not be used when impurity spreads beyond the exit area?
b: Because wiping does not remove impurity sufficiently in that case; the allowance of stones is restricted to the normal place of istinjāʾ.

f: 602. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, how is excess impurity beyond the exit area measured?
b: The amount beyond the normal exit area is considered, because the exit area itself is overlooked.

f: 603. According to Muḥammad, how is excess impurity beyond the exit area measured?
b: The normal exit area is also included in the calculation, similar to other areas.

f: 604. Is istinjāʾ with bones permitted?
b: No, it is prohibited because the Prophet ﷺ forbade it.

f: 605. If someone uses a bone for istinjāʾ, is the purification valid according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes, because the purpose of removing impurity is achieved, although the action is disliked.

f: 606. Why is using bones for istinjāʾ prohibited?
b: Because bones are considered the provision of the jinn.

f: 607. Is istinjāʾ with animal dung permitted?
b: No, it is prohibited because the Prophet ﷺ forbade it.

f: 608. Why is using animal dung for istinjāʾ prohibited?
b: Because dung itself is impure.

f: 609. Is istinjāʾ with food permitted?
b: No, it is prohibited.

f: 610. Why is using food for istinjāʾ prohibited?
b: Because it is considered wastefulness and improper disposal of a blessing.

f: 611. Is it permissible to clean oneself after relieving oneself with the right hand?
b: No, it is prohibited.

f: 612. What evidence is mentioned for avoiding the right hand in istinjāʾ?
b: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited performing istinjāʾ with the right hand.

f: 1. What is the beginning time of Fajr according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: The time of Fajr begins when the second (true) dawn appears, which is the horizontal whiteness spreading across the horizon.

f: 2. What is the end time of Fajr according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: The end time of Fajr is before the sun rises.

f: 3. What evidence is used for the beginning and end times of Fajr?
b: The ḥadīth of Jibrīl عليه السلام, who led the Prophet ﷺ in prayer on the first day at the appearance of dawn and on the second day when it became very bright before sunrise, then said: “Between these two times is the time for you and your الأمة.”

f: 4. What is the false dawn (al-fajr al-kādhib)?
b: It is a vertical whiteness that appears in the sky and is followed by darkness.

f: 5. Is the false dawn considered the beginning of Fajr prayer time?
b: No, it is not considered because the Prophet ﷺ said that the true dawn is the whiteness spreading across the horizon.

f: 6. What is the beginning time of Ẓuhr prayer?
b: The time of Ẓuhr begins when the sun passes its zenith (zawāl).

f: 7. What evidence is used for the beginning time of Ẓuhr?
b: Jibrīl عليه السلام led the Prophet ﷺ in prayer on the first day when the sun had passed its zenith.

f: 8. When does the time of Ẓuhr end according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: The time of Ẓuhr ends when the shadow of every object becomes twice its original length, excluding the shadow at midday (fayʾ al-zawāl).

f: 9. When does the time of Ẓuhr end according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: It ends when the shadow of every object becomes equal to its original length, excluding the midday shadow.

f: 10. What evidence do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad use for ending Ẓuhr at one shadow length?
b: The narration of Jibrīl’s prayer, as he prayed Ẓuhr on the first day at that time.

f: 11. What evidence does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله use for delaying Ẓuhr until two shadow lengths?
b: The Prophet’s ﷺ statement: “Cool down the Ẓuhr prayer, for intense heat is from the breath of Hell.”

f: 12. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله not end Ẓuhr time based on the earlier narration?
b: Because when evidences conflict, the prayer time is not removed by doubt.

f: 13. When does the time of ʿAṣr begin according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: It begins when the time of Ẓuhr ends according to either opinion.

f: 14. When does the time of ʿAṣr end?
b: It ends before sunset.

f: 15. What evidence is used for the end of ʿAṣr time?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever catches one rakʿah of ʿAṣr before sunset has caught ʿAṣr.”

f: 16. When does Maghrib time begin?
b: Maghrib begins immediately after the sun sets.

f: 17. When does Maghrib time end according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: It ends when the twilight (shafaq) disappears.

f: 18. What is the opinion of al-Shāfiʿī regarding the end of Maghrib time?
b: He holds that Maghrib time lasts only long enough to pray three rakʿahs.

f: 19. What evidence does al-Shāfiʿī use for limiting Maghrib time?
b: Jibrīl عليه السلام prayed Maghrib at the same time on both days.

f: 20. What evidence do the Ḥanafīs use for extending Maghrib until twilight disappears?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The beginning of Maghrib is when the sun sets and its end is when the twilight disappears.”

f: 21. What did the Ḥanafīs say regarding the narration used by al-Shāfiʿī?
b: They said it was intended to avoid disliked delay, not to define the entire prayer time.

f: 22. What is the definition of twilight (shafaq) according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: It is the whiteness that remains in the horizon after the redness disappears.

f: 23. What is the definition of twilight according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, Muḥammad, and al-Shāfiʿī?
b: It is the redness that appears after sunset.

f: 24. What evidence do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, Muḥammad, and al-Shāfiʿī use for defining twilight as redness?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The twilight is the redness.”

f: 25. What evidence does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله use for defining twilight as whiteness?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The end of Maghrib is when the horizon becomes dark.”

f: 26. What is the beginning time of ʿIshāʾ prayer?
b: ʿIshāʾ begins when the twilight disappears.

f: 27. What is the end time of ʿIshāʾ prayer?
b: The end time is before the second dawn appears.

f: 28. What evidence is used for the end of ʿIshāʾ time?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The end of the time of ʿIshāʾ is when dawn appears.”

f: 29. What is the opinion of al-Shāfiʿī regarding the end of ʿIshāʾ time?
b: He considers it to end after one-third of the night.

f: 30. When does the time of Witr begin according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: It begins after ʿIshāʾ prayer and ends at the appearance of Fajr.

f: 31. When does the time of Witr begin according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Its time is the same as the time of ʿIshāʾ, although it should not be prayed before ʿIshāʾ when the order is remembered.

f: 32. What is the recommended practice regarding the timing of Fajr prayer?
b: It is recommended to delay Fajr until it becomes light (isfār).

f: 33. What evidence is used for delaying Fajr?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Perform Fajr when it becomes light, for it brings greater reward.”

f: 34. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding delaying Fajr?
b: He recommends praying every prayer at its earliest time.

f: 35. What is the recommended practice for Ẓuhr prayer in summer?
b: It is recommended to delay Ẓuhr until the heat decreases (ibrād).

f: 36. What is the recommended practice for Ẓuhr prayer in winter?
b: It is recommended to pray Ẓuhr earlier.

f: 37. What evidence is used for delaying Ẓuhr in summer and advancing it in winter?
b: Anas رضي الله عنه reported that the Prophet ﷺ prayed Ẓuhr early in winter and delayed it in summer.

f: 38. What is the recommended timing for ʿAṣr prayer?
b: It is recommended to delay ʿAṣr until before the sun changes color, in both summer and winter.

f: 39. What does “the sun changes color” mean in relation to ʿAṣr prayer?
b: It means the sun becomes weak enough that the eyes can look at its disk without difficulty.

f: 40. Is delaying ʿAṣr until the sun changes color disliked?
b: Yes, delaying it until that point is disliked.

f: 41. What is the recommended timing for Maghrib prayer?
b: It is recommended to pray Maghrib immediately after sunset.

f: 42. Why is delaying Maghrib disliked?
b: Because it resembles the practice of the Jews.

f: 43. What did the Prophet ﷺ say regarding hastening Maghrib and delaying ʿIshāʾ?
b: “My الأمة will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten Maghrib and delay ʿIshāʾ.”

f: 44. What is the recommended time for ʿIshāʾ prayer?
b: It is recommended to delay ʿIshāʾ until before one-third of the night.

f: 45. What evidence supports delaying ʿIshāʾ until one-third of the night?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If it were not hardship upon my الأمة, I would have delayed ʿIshāʾ until one-third of the night.”

f: 46. Why is delaying ʿIshāʾ beneficial?
b: It reduces unnecessary night conversation (samar) after the prayer.

f: 47. Is delaying ʿIshāʾ until half the night permissible?
b: Yes, it is permissible.

f: 48. Why is delaying ʿIshāʾ until half the night considered permissible?
b: The dislike of reducing congregation conflicts with the benefit of ending night gatherings, so the ruling becomes permissibility.

f: 49. Is delaying ʿIshāʾ beyond half the night disliked?
b: Yes, because it reduces congregation and the benefit of ending night gatherings has already been achieved.

f: 50. When should someone who regularly performs night prayer pray Witr?
b: They should delay Witr until the end of the night.

f: 51. When should someone who fears not waking for night prayer pray Witr?
b: They should pray Witr before sleeping.

f: 52. What evidence supports delaying Witr for those confident of waking?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever fears he will not rise at the end of the night should pray Witr at its beginning, and whoever hopes to rise should pray it at its end.”

f: 53. What is recommended on a cloudy day regarding Fajr, Ẓuhr, and Maghrib prayers?
b: It is recommended to delay them.

f: 54. What is recommended on a cloudy day regarding ʿAṣr and ʿIshāʾ prayers?
b: It is recommended to pray them earlier.

f: 55. Why is ʿIshāʾ delayed on a cloudy day according to the text?
b: Because delaying it could reduce congregation due to assuming rain or difficulty.

f: 56. Why is ʿAṣr hastened on a cloudy day?
b: Because there is a fear of accidentally entering the disliked time of ʿAṣr.

f: 57. Why is Fajr not hastened on a cloudy day?
b: Because its time period is long, so there is less fear of missing it.

f: 58. What was another opinion transmitted from Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله regarding cloudy days?
b: He preferred delaying all prayers as a precaution.

f: 59. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله prefer delaying all prayers on cloudy days?
b: Because performing a prayer after its time is possible, but performing it before its time is not.

f: 60. At which three times is prayer not permitted according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: Prayer is not permitted at sunrise, when the sun is at its zenith (midday), and at sunset.

f: 61. What evidence is used for the prohibition of prayer at sunrise, midday, and sunset?
b: The ḥadīth of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir رضي الله عنه that the Prophet ﷺ forbade prayer and burying the dead at these three times.

f: 62. What is meant by the phrase “burying our dead” in the ḥadīth about prohibited times?
b: It refers to the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah), not the actual burial.

f: 63. Is actual burial of the deceased disliked during the prohibited prayer times?
b: No, the actual burial is not disliked.

f: 64. Is the prohibition of these times limited to obligatory prayers according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, the prohibition applies generally and is a proof against al-Shāfiʿī’s restriction of it to certain prayers.

f: 65. Does the prohibition of these times apply in Makkah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes, it applies even in Makkah for voluntary prayers, contrary to al-Shāfiʿī’s view.

f: 66. Does the prohibition at midday prevent voluntary prayer on Friday according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes, contrary to Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله opinion allowing voluntary prayer at midday on Friday.

f: 67. Can the funeral prayer be performed during the prohibited times?
b: It is disliked during these times.

f: 68. Can a prostration of recitation (sajdat al-tilāwah) be performed during the prohibited times?
b: It is disliked because it has the ruling of prayer.

f: 69. Why is the ʿAṣr prayer of the same day allowed at sunset despite the prohibition?
b: Because the cause of its obligation is connected to the remaining portion of its time; performing it at the end of the time is considered performance, not making up (qaḍāʾ).

f: 70. Why are other prayers not allowed at sunset while the ʿAṣr of that day is allowed?
b: Other prayers became obligatory as complete acts, so they cannot be fulfilled in a deficient manner, whereas ʿAṣr was already due based on the remaining part of its time.

f: 71. Is the prohibition of funeral prayer and sajdat al-tilāwah during these times absolute invalidity or merely dislike?
b: It means dislike; if performed during these times, it is valid.

f: 72. Why are funeral prayer and sajdat al-tilāwah valid if performed during disliked times?
b: Because they are performed as they became obligatory: the funeral prayer due to the presence of the deceased and sajdat al-tilāwah due to reciting the verse of prostration.

f: 73. Is voluntary prayer allowed after Fajr until sunrise?
b: No, voluntary prayer is disliked after Fajr until sunrise.

f: 74. Is voluntary prayer allowed after ʿAṣr until sunset?
b: No, voluntary prayer is disliked after ʿAṣr until sunset.

f: 75. What evidence is used for the dislike of voluntary prayer after Fajr and ʿAṣr?
b: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited voluntary prayers during these times.

f: 76. Are missed obligatory prayers (farāʾiḍ) allowed after Fajr and after ʿAṣr?
b: Yes, making up missed obligatory prayers is allowed during these times.

f: 77. Is sajdat al-tilāwah allowed after Fajr and after ʿAṣr?
b: Yes, it is allowed.

f: 78. Is funeral prayer allowed after Fajr and after ʿAṣr?
b: Yes, it is allowed.

f: 79. Why does the dislike of voluntary prayer after Fajr and ʿAṣr not apply to missed obligatory prayers?
b: Because the dislike is due to making the time appear occupied with an obligatory prayer, not because of the time itself.

f: 80. Why is sajdat al-tilāwah allowed after Fajr and ʿAṣr?
b: Because it becomes obligatory due to the specific cause of reciting the verse of prostration.

f: 81. Why is a vowed voluntary prayer (nadhr) disliked after Fajr and ʿAṣr?
b: Because its obligation arose from a person’s own action, not from an external cause like a funeral or recitation.

f: 82. Why are the two rakʿahs after ṭawāf disliked after Fajr and ʿAṣr?
b: Because their obligation comes from completing the ṭawāf, not from the time itself.

f: 83. Why is a prayer that was started and then invalidated disliked to repeat after Fajr and ʿAṣr?
b: Because its obligation came from preserving the original act after it was started, not because of the time.

f: 84. How many voluntary rakʿahs are disliked after the appearance of Fajr?
b: More than the two rakʿahs of the Fajr sunnah are disliked.

f: 85. Why is praying more than two rakʿahs after Fajr disliked?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ did not add to the two rakʿahs of Fajr despite his eagerness for prayer.

f: 86. Is voluntary prayer allowed between sunset and Maghrib prayer?
b: No, it is disliked because it delays the obligatory Maghrib prayer.

f: 87. Is voluntary prayer allowed after the Friday imām comes out to deliver the sermon?
b: No, it is disliked until the sermon ends because it distracts from listening to the khuṭbah.

f: 88. What is the ruling of the adhān according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: The adhān is a sunnah for the five daily prayers and Friday prayer only.

f: 89. Why is adhān considered a sunnah for the five prayers and Friday prayer?
b: Because this practice has been transmitted through continuous widespread reports (tawātur).

f: 90. Is there tarjiʿ (repeating the testimony loudly after saying it quietly) in the adhān according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, there is no tarjiʿ in the adhān.

f: 91. What is tarjiʿ in the adhān?
b: It is repeating the two testimonies loudly after first saying them quietly.

f: 92. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding tarjiʿ in the adhān?
b: He considers tarjiʿ part of the adhān based on the report of Abū Maḥdhūrah رضي الله عنه.

f: 93. How do the Ḥanafīs respond to the narration about tarjiʿ?
b: They say it was for teaching the words of the adhān, and Abū Maḥdhūrah misunderstood it as tarjiʿ.

f: 94. What phrase is added to the Fajr adhān after “Ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ”?
b: “Al-ṣalātu khayrun min al-nawm” (Prayer is better than sleep), twice.

f: 95. Why is “Prayer is better than sleep” added specifically to the Fajr adhān?
b: Because Fajr is a time when people are sleeping and less attentive.

f: 96. What is the ruling of the iqāmah compared to the adhān?
b: The iqāmah is like the adhān except that “Qad qāmat al-ṣalāh” is added twice after “Ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ.”

f: 97. How does the Ḥanafī iqāmah differ from al-Shāfiʿī’s view?
b: The Ḥanafīs say the phrases are repeated twice, while al-Shāfiʿī says they are said once except “Qad qāmat al-ṣalāh.”

f: 98. How should the adhān be recited?
b: Slowly and clearly (tarassul).

f: 99. How should the iqāmah be recited?
b: Quickly (ḥadr).

f: 100. What evidence is mentioned for reciting the adhān slowly and iqāmah quickly?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told Bilāl رضي الله عنه: “When you give adhān, recite slowly; when you give iqāmah, recite quickly.”

f: 101. Should the caller to prayer face the qiblah during adhān and iqāmah?
b: Yes, it is recommended.

f: 102. Why should the muʾadhdhin face the qiblah?
b: Because the angel who gave the adhān did so facing the qiblah.

f: 103. Is the adhān valid if the muʾadhdhin does not face the qiblah?
b: Yes, because the purpose of the adhān is still achieved, though it opposes the sunnah.

f: 104. When saying “Ḥayya ʿala al-ṣalāh” and “Ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ,” where should the muʾadhdhin turn?
b: He should turn his face right and left.

f: 105. Why does the muʾadhdhin turn his face during “Ḥayya ʿala al-ṣalāh” and “Ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ”?
b: Because these phrases address the people, so he faces them.

f: 106. Is turning the whole body during adhān recommended?
b: It is acceptable if needed, such as when standing in a narrow minaret, while keeping the feet in place.

f: 107. What is the preferred practice regarding placing fingers in the ears during adhān?
b: It is preferred for the muʾadhdhin to place his fingers in his ears.

f: 108. Why should the muʾadhdhin place his fingers in his ears?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ instructed Bilāl رضي الله عنه to do so and it helps make the voice louder.

f: 109. Is placing fingers in the ears an essential sunnah of adhān?
b: No, if he does not do it, it is still acceptable.

f: 110. What is tathwīb in the Fajr adhān?
b: Saying “Ḥayya ʿala al-ṣalāh, Ḥayya ʿala al-falāḥ” twice between the adhān and iqāmah.

f: 111. Why is tathwīb in Fajr considered good?
b: Because Fajr is a time of sleep and heedlessness.

f: 112. Is tathwīb recommended in prayers other than Fajr according to the earlier Ḥanafī view?
b: No, it is disliked in other prayers.

f: 113. What does tathwīb mean linguistically?
b: Returning to calling people after they have already been called.

f: 114. Who introduced tathwīb according to the text?
b: The scholars of Kūfah introduced it after the era of the Companions due to changes in people’s circumstances.

f: 115. Why was tathwīb originally restricted to Fajr?
b: Because Fajr is specifically a time of sleep and reduced awareness.

f: 116. What did later scholars prefer regarding tathwīb?
b: They considered it good in all prayers because people became more negligent in religious matters.

f: 117. What did Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله say regarding the muʾadhdhin addressing the ruler before the adhān?
b: He said he sees no problem with the muʾadhdhin saying to the ruler in all prayers: “Peace be upon you, O leader, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Come to prayer, come to success. Prayer, may Allah have mercy upon you.”

f: 118. Why did Muḥammad object to the muʾadhdhin giving a special call to the ruler?
b: Because people are equal regarding attending the congregational prayer.

f: 119. Why did Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله allow addressing the ruler specially before prayer?
b: Because rulers are more occupied with the affairs of Muslims, so this reminder helps prevent them from missing the congregation.

f: 120. Does the same ruling apply to judges and scholars according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: Yes, because they are also occupied with important responsibilities.

f: 121. Should there be a sitting period between the adhān and iqāmah according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, a sitting period should occur between them except for Maghrib.

f: 122. Should there be a sitting period between adhān and iqāmah for Maghrib according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: Yes, but it should be a brief sitting.

f: 123. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad require a separation between Maghrib adhān and iqāmah?
b: Because joining them directly is disliked, and a pause alone is not enough since pauses already exist between the words of the adhān.

f: 124. How do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad compare the separation between adhān and iqāmah to another practice?
b: They compare it to the sitting between the two Friday sermons.

f: 125. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله not require a sitting period before Maghrib?
b: Because delaying Maghrib is disliked, so the smallest separation is sufficient.

f: 126. How does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله view the pause between adhān and iqāmah in Maghrib?
b: He considers the pause sufficient because the place and melody differ from the pauses within the adhān itself.

f: 127. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding the separation between adhān and iqāmah?
b: He recommends separating them with two rakʿahs, comparing Maghrib with other prayers.

f: 128. What did Yaʿqūb report seeing Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله do regarding Maghrib adhān and iqāmah?
b: He saw Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله give the adhān and immediately establish the iqāmah without sitting between them.

f: 129. What does the report of Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله giving Maghrib adhān and iqāmah without sitting indicate?
b: It indicates that the preferred practice is what Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله stated regarding Maghrib.

f: 130. What quality should a muʾadhdhin ideally have according to the text?
b: He should know the Sunnah.

f: 131. What evidence is mentioned that the muʾadhdhin should be knowledgeable?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Let the best among you give the adhān.”

f: 132. What is the ruling for making adhān and iqāmah for a missed prayer?
b: Adhān and iqāmah are performed for it.

f: 133. What evidence is used for making adhān and iqāmah for a missed prayer?
b: The Prophet ﷺ made adhān and iqāmah when he made up the missed Fajr after the journey of al-Taʿrīs.

f: 134. What is the Ḥanafī response to al-Shāfiʿī’s view that only iqāmah is needed for missed prayers?
b: The report of the Prophet ﷺ performing both adhān and iqāmah proves both are prescribed.

f: 135. If several prayers are missed, what should a person do regarding adhān and iqāmah?
b: He gives adhān for the first missed prayer and iqāmah for each prayer.

f: 136. If several prayers are missed, is the person required to give adhān for every prayer according to the main Ḥanafī view?
b: No, he has a choice: he may give adhān and iqāmah for each, or only iqāmah after the first.

f: 137. Why may someone performing multiple missed prayers only use iqāmah after the first?
b: Because the purpose of adhān is to call absent people, while those making up prayers are already present.

f: 138. What was another narration from Muḥammad regarding multiple missed prayers?
b: He said iqāmah should be made for the following prayers without adhān.

f: 139. Should adhān and iqāmah be performed while in a state of ritual purity?
b: It is recommended to perform them while purified.

f: 140. Is adhān valid if someone gives it without wuḍūʾ?
b: Yes, because adhān is remembrance (dhikr), not prayer.

f: 141. Why is wuḍūʾ recommended for adhān but not required?
b: Because adhān resembles recitation of Qurʾān, where purity is recommended.

f: 142. Is it disliked to give iqāmah without wuḍūʾ?
b: Yes, according to the main narration.

f: 143. Why is giving iqāmah without wuḍūʾ disliked?
b: Because it creates separation between the iqāmah and the prayer.

f: 144. Is there another narration regarding iqāmah without wuḍūʾ?
b: Yes, it states that it is not disliked because iqāmah is one of the two forms of adhān.

f: 145. Why is giving adhān while junub disliked according to one explanation?
b: Because adhān has some resemblance to prayer, and therefore requires purification from the greater ritual impurity.

f: 146. Is giving adhān while junub disliked according to all narrations?
b: Yes, it is disliked according to all narrations.

f: 147. If someone gives adhān and iqāmah without wuḍūʾ, must they repeat them?
b: No, repeating them is not required.

f: 148. If someone gives adhān and iqāmah while junub, is repeating them preferred?
b: Yes, repeating the adhān is preferred; the ruling regarding repeating iqāmah differs.

f: 149. Why is repeating adhān preferred for someone who was junub?
b: Because repeating adhān is legislated, unlike repeating iqāmah.

f: 150. If someone does not repeat the adhān after giving it while junub, is the prayer valid?
b: Yes, because the prayer is valid without adhān and iqāmah.

f: 151. What does the statement “likewise the woman gives adhān” mean?
b: It means it is recommended to repeat the adhān so that it occurs according to the Sunnah.

f: 152. Is adhān valid before the prayer time begins?
b: No, adhān before the time begins is not valid and should be repeated after the time enters.

f: 153. Why is adhān before the prayer time invalid?
b: Because adhān is meant to inform people of the prayer time, and before the time it gives incorrect information.

f: 154. What was Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله opinion regarding Fajr adhān before its time?
b: He allowed it in the second half of the night, and this is also the opinion of al-Shāfiʿī.

f: 155. What evidence is used against giving Fajr adhān before its proper time?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told Bilāl رضي الله عنه: “Do not give adhān until dawn becomes clear for you,” while stretching his hand horizontally.

f: 156. What should a traveler do regarding adhān and iqāmah?
b: A traveler should give both adhān and iqāmah.

f: 157. What evidence supports travelers giving adhān and iqāmah?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told the two sons of Abū Mulaykah رضي الله عنهما: “When you travel, give adhān and iqāmah.”

f: 158. What is the ruling if a traveler leaves both adhān and iqāmah?
b: It is disliked.

f: 159. If a traveler leaves adhān but gives iqāmah, is the prayer valid?
b: Yes, because the companions are already present and do not need the call.

f: 160. Why is adhān more connected to absent people while iqāmah is needed by those present?
b: Adhān calls people to attend, while iqāmah announces the beginning of the prayer.

f: 161. If someone prays alone at home in a town, should they give adhān and iqāmah?
b: Yes, it is recommended to do so.

f: 162. Why should someone praying alone at home in a town give adhān and iqāmah?
b: To make their prayer resemble the manner of congregational prayer.

f: 163. Is prayer valid if someone praying alone in town leaves adhān and iqāmah?
b: Yes, it is valid.

f: 164. What statement of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه is used regarding leaving adhān and iqāmah when praying at home?
b: “The adhān of the people of the town is sufficient for us.”

f: 165. What must a person do before beginning prayer regarding ritual impurities?
b: They must first purify themselves from minor and major ritual impurities.

f: 166. What evidence is given for requiring purification before prayer?
b: The verses: “Purify your garments” and “If you are in a state of janābah, then purify yourselves.”

f: 167. What must a person do regarding covering the body before prayer?
b: They must cover their ʿawrah.

f: 168. What evidence is given for covering the ʿawrah during prayer?
b: Allah’s statement: “Take your adornment at every place of prayer,” meaning what covers your nakedness.

f: 169. What does the ḥadīth “There is no prayer for a menstruating woman except with a khimār” mean?
b: It refers to an adult woman needing to cover herself during prayer.

f: 170. What is the ʿawrah of a man according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: The area from below the navel to below the knees.

f: 171. What evidence is used for defining the man’s ʿawrah?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The ʿawrah of a man is what is between his navel and knees.”

f: 172. Is the navel itself part of the man’s ʿawrah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, the navel is not part of the ʿawrah.

f: 173. Is the knee part of the man’s ʿawrah according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Yes, the knee is part of the ʿawrah.

f: 174. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding the navel and knee?
b: He differs by not considering the knee part of the ʿawrah and by differing regarding the navel.

f: 175. What parts of a free woman's body are considered awrah during prayer according to al-Hidayah?
b: The entire body of a free woman is awrah except her face and hands. This is based on the hadith that "the woman is awrah and concealed," while the face and hands are excluded due to the need to expose them.

f: 176. According to the preferred view in the Hanafi school, are a woman's feet considered awrah?
b: The preferred view is that a woman's feet are not awrah, although there is another narration stating that they are awrah.

f: 177. According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله and Muhammad, what is the ruling if a woman prays while a quarter of her leg is uncovered?
b: She must repeat the prayer if a quarter of her leg is uncovered. If less than a quarter is uncovered, she does not repeat the prayer.

f: 178. According to Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, when does a woman need to repeat the prayer due to part of her awrah being uncovered?
b: Abu Yusuf رحمه الله holds that she does not repeat the prayer unless less than half of her awrah is covered (i.e., half or more is uncovered).

f: 179. Why did Abu Hanifah رحمه الله and Muhammad consider one quarter of the body as the amount requiring repetition of the prayer?
b: Because one quarter represents the whole in certain rulings, such as wiping a quarter of the head in wudu and removing a quarter of the hair during ihram violations.

f: 180. Are a woman's hair, stomach, and thigh treated like other awrah parts regarding the amount that invalidates the prayer?
b: Yes. The same disagreement applies to these parts regarding whether one quarter or one half being exposed requires repeating the prayer.

f: 181. What is meant by the hair being awrah in the discussion of a woman's prayer?
b: It refers to the hair descending from the head. Its being washed during ghusl is prescribed due to difficulty, not because it is outside the awrah.

f: 182. Is the male private part considered separately when determining awrah exposure?
b: Yes. The male organ and testicles are each considered separately according to the correct view, rather than being combined as one area.

f: 183. What parts of a female slave's body are considered awrah according to al-Hidayah?
b: The same parts that are awrah for a man are awrah for a female slave. Additionally, her stomach and back are awrah, while the rest of her body is not considered awrah.

f: 184. Why is the awrah ruling for a female slave different from that of a free woman?
b: Because female slaves traditionally worked and moved about for their masters' needs, so their ruling was made similar to women who are mahram to men in order to remove hardship.

f: 185. What should a person do if they cannot remove impurity from their clothing before prayer?
b: They pray while carrying the impurity and do not repeat the prayer.

f: 186. If a person has a clean quarter or more of their garment available, what should they do when they cannot remove impurity?
b: They must pray wearing the clean part, because a quarter of something can represent the whole in some rulings.

f: 187. According to Imam Muhammad رحمه الله, what should a person do if less than a quarter of their clothing is clean but the rest is impure?
b: They should still pray wearing it, because praying with impurity is considered less problematic than praying completely naked.

f: 188. According to Abu Hanifah رحمه الله and Abu Yusuf رحمه الله, what choice does a person have if less than a quarter of their garment is clean and the rest is impure?
b: They may either pray naked or pray wearing the impure garment, although praying with the garment is preferable.

f: 189. Why is praying naked not automatically preferred when someone cannot remove impurity from clothing?
b: Because both impurity and lack of clothing prevent valid prayer in normal circumstances, and neither option has absolute priority in this situation.

f: 190. What should someone do if they have no clothing at all and must pray?
b: They should pray sitting and gesture for bowing and prostration.

f: 191. If someone without clothing prays standing instead of sitting, is the prayer valid?
b: Yes, the prayer is valid, because standing fulfills the pillars of prayer while sitting provides greater concealment.

f: 192. Which option is considered better for someone without clothing: praying sitting or standing?
b: Praying sitting is better because covering the awrah is required for the sake of prayer and people's rights, while gestures replace the physical movements.

f: 193. What is required regarding intention before beginning prayer?
b: A person must intend the specific prayer they are entering before the opening takbir, without performing an action that separates the intention from the prayer.

f: 194. Why is intention required before prayer according to al-Hidayah?
b: Because actions are judged by intentions, and standing before prayer could be either a habit or an act of worship, so intention distinguishes between them.

f: 195. Is verbalizing the intention for prayer necessary?
b: No. The intention is the action of the heart. Saying it verbally is only beneficial for gathering one's resolve.

f: 196. What must a person know in their intention when praying a fard prayer?
b: They must specify which obligatory prayer they are performing, such as Dhuhr, because the obligatory prayers differ.

f: 197. Is a general intention sufficient for voluntary prayers?
b: Yes. A general intention is sufficient for nafl prayers and, according to the correct view, also for sunnah prayers.

f: 198. What intention must an imam's follower (muqtadi) make when joining another person in prayer?
b: They must intend the prayer and intend following the imam because their prayer depends on the imam's actions.

f: 199. What is the ruling on facing the qiblah during prayer?
b: Facing the qiblah is obligatory based on Allah's command: "Turn your faces toward it."

f: 200. What is the difference between the obligation of facing the qiblah for someone in Makkah and someone far away?
b: Someone in Makkah must face the actual Ka'bah, while someone far away must face the direction of the Ka'bah according to the correct view.

f: 201. What should a person do if they are afraid and cannot face the qiblah normally?
b: They pray facing whatever direction they are able to face due to the excuse, similar to a person unable to determine the qiblah.

f: 202. What should a person do if they cannot determine the qiblah and nobody is available to ask?
b: They should perform their own investigation (ijtihad) and pray according to the direction they believe is correct.

f: 203. Why is a person allowed to rely on their own investigation when the qiblah is unknown?
b: Because acting upon the strongest available evidence is required when no higher evidence is available.

f: 204. If someone discovers after prayer that they faced the wrong direction while they had investigated, must they repeat the prayer?
b: No. They do not repeat because they acted according to their ability and were not responsible for what was beyond their knowledge.

f: 205. According to al-Hidayah, does a person repeat the prayer if they knowingly discover during prayer that the qiblah direction was wrong?
b: No. They turn toward the qiblah and continue the prayer from where they are.

f: 206. What evidence is given that a person who discovers the qiblah direction during prayer should turn and continue?
b: The people of Quba were informed that the qiblah had changed while they were praying, so they turned toward it and the Prophet ﷺ approved of their action.

f: 207. If a person's opinion about the qiblah changes during prayer due to stronger evidence, what should they do?
b: They should turn toward the new direction and continue the prayer without repeating what has already been performed.

f: 208. What happens if an imam leads people on a dark night, investigates the qiblah, prays facing east, and those behind him also investigate but each faces a different direction without knowing the imam's direction?
b: Their prayer is valid because each person faced the direction reached through their own investigation. This difference does not invalidate the prayer, just as it does not invalidate prayer inside the Kaʿbah.

f: 209. When does the prayer of someone following the imam become invalid in the case of uncertainty about the qiblah?
b: If a person knows that the imam is facing the wrong direction, his prayer becomes invalid because he believes his imam is mistaken.

f: 210. What other situation invalidates the prayer of a follower behind the imam regarding position?
b: If the follower stands ahead of the imam, his prayer is invalid because he has abandoned the required position of following the imam.

f: 211. How many obligatory components (farāʾiḍ) does prayer have according to al-Hidāyah?
b: Prayer has six obligatory components: the opening takbīr, standing, recitation, bowing, prostration, and the final sitting for the duration of the tashahhud.

f: 212. What is the evidence that the opening takbīr is an obligatory component of prayer?
b: Allah's statement: "And magnify your Lord" (Qur'an 74:3). The intended meaning is the takbīr that begins the prayer.

f: 213. What is the evidence that standing is an obligatory component of prayer?
b: Allah's statement: "Stand before Allah devoutly" (Qur'an 2:238).

f: 214. What is the evidence that recitation is an obligatory component of prayer?
b: Allah's statement: "Recite whatever is easy of the Qur'an" (Qur'an 73:20).

f: 215. What is the evidence that bowing and prostration are obligatory components of prayer?
b: Allah's statement: "Bow and prostrate" (Qur'an 22:77).

f: 216. What is the evidence that the final sitting for the duration of tashahhud is an obligatory component of prayer?
b: The Prophet ﷺ taught Ibn Masʿūd the tashahhud and said that after saying it or doing it, the prayer is complete, indicating that the sitting itself completes the prayer.

f: 217. What are the acts that are considered sunnah in prayer according to al-Hidāyah?
b: Everything besides the six pillars is called sunnah in the text, although some of these are actually obligations established through the Sunnah.

f: 218. Which acts in prayer are obligations (wājibāt) despite being called sunnah in al-Hidāyah?
b: They include reciting al-Fātiḥah, adding another sūrah after it, maintaining order in repeated actions, the first sitting, reciting tashahhud in the final sitting, qunūt in witr, the additional takbīrs of the two Eids, reciting aloud in audible prayers, and reciting quietly in silent prayers.

f: 219. Why are some obligatory acts called sunnah in al-Hidāyah?
b: Because their obligation is established through the Sunnah rather than directly through the Qur'an.

f: 220. What should a person do when beginning the prayer?
b: He should say the opening takbīr.

f: 221. Is the opening takbīr a condition (sharṭ) or a pillar (rukn) according to the Hanafis?
b: According to the Hanafis, the opening takbīr is a condition of entering the prayer, not one of the repeated pillars of prayer.

f: 222. What is the evidence that the opening takbīr is a condition rather than a pillar according to the Hanafis?
b: Allah says: "And mention the name of his Lord and pray" (Qur'an 87:15), which separates mentioning Allah's name from prayer, showing that the takbīr is distinct from the prayer itself.

f: 223. What is the Shafiʿi position regarding the opening takbīr?
b: The Shafiʿis consider it part of the prayer itself, requiring the same conditions as other pillars.

f: 224. Can someone who made the opening takbīr intending an obligatory prayer use that same prayer to perform a voluntary prayer according to the Hanafis?
b: Yes, according to the Hanafis, because the opening takbīr is separate from the prayer itself.

f: 225. What is the ruling on raising the hands when saying the opening takbīr?
b: Raising the hands is a sunnah because the Prophet ﷺ consistently did so.

f: 226. What is the correct order regarding raising the hands and saying takbīr?
b: The more correct view is that one raises the hands first and then says the takbīr.

f: 227. Why is raising the hands before the takbīr considered preferable?
b: Because raising the hands negates greatness from everything besides Allah, and negation precedes affirmation.

f: 228. How high should a man raise his hands during the opening takbīr according to the Hanafi school?
b: He raises them until his thumbs reach the level of his earlobes.

f: 229. What is the Shafiʿi position on how high to raise the hands during takbīr?
b: The Shafiʿis hold that the hands should be raised to the shoulders.

f: 230. What is the Hanafi evidence for raising the hands to the ears rather than the shoulders?
b: Reports from Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr, al-Barāʾ, and Anas رضي الله عنهم state that the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands level with his ears when saying takbīr.

f: 231. Why did the Hanafis interpret reports mentioning the shoulders differently?
b: They interpreted them as referring to a situation of necessity or a particular circumstance.

f: 232. How should a woman raise her hands during the opening takbīr according to the Hanafi school?
b: She raises them level with her shoulders because this is more concealing for her.

f: 233. Does saying a phrase other than "Allāhu Akbar" invalidate the opening takbīr according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: No. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad, other expressions of Allah's greatness, such as "Allāhu Ajall" or "Allāhu Aʿẓam," are sufficient.

f: 234. What is Abū Yūsuf's رحمه الله position regarding expressions used instead of "Allāhu Akbar"?
b: If a person knows how to say "Allāhu Akbar," only phrases such as "Allāhu Akbar," "Allāhu al-Akbar," or "Allāhu al-Kabīr" are valid according to him.

f: 235. What is al-Shāfiʿī's position regarding replacing "Allāhu Akbar" in the opening takbīr?
b: He holds that only the first two expressions are valid.

f: 236. What is Mālik's position regarding the opening takbīr?
b: Mālik holds that only "Allāhu Akbar" is valid because it is the transmitted wording.

f: 237. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad allow other expressions besides "Allāhu Akbar"?
b: Because the linguistic meaning of takbīr is glorification, and that meaning is achieved through other expressions.

f: 238. What is the ruling if someone begins prayer, recites Qur'an, or slaughters an animal using Persian while knowing Arabic?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, it is valid. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad, it is not valid for prayer recitation or opening the prayer, although they allow it for slaughter.

f: 239. What is the ruling if someone does not know Arabic and uses Persian for the opening takbīr or recitation?
b: It is valid according to all of them because he is unable to use Arabic.

f: 240. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad not allow Qur'an recitation in another language when someone knows Arabic?
b: Because the Qur'an refers to the Arabic wording itself, as indicated by the revelation, and translation is only accepted in cases of inability.

f: 241. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله allow recitation in another language?
b: Because Allah mentions that the Qur'an existed in earlier scriptures, which were not in Arabic; therefore, the meaning can represent the Qur'an when necessary.

f: 242. Is reciting the Qur'an in another language considered ideal according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No. Although valid, it is considered blameworthy because it opposes the established Sunnah of reciting in Arabic.

f: 243. Can prayer recitation be performed in languages other than Persian according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, this is the correct view according to him based on the same reasoning.

f: 244. Is the validity of saying the opening takbīr in prayer affected by different languages?
b: No. The meaning does not differ between languages, and the disagreement is only regarding whether it counts as sufficient. There is no disagreement that using another language does not invalidate the prayer.

f: 245. What is the relied-upon position regarding opening the prayer in a language other than Arabic?
b: The relied-upon position is that it is valid, although some narrations mention that Imām Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله later returned to the view of his two companions (Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad).

f: 246. Does the ruling of using another language apply to the opening takbīr, recitation, the testimony (tashahhud), and the khuṭbah?
b: Yes, the same disagreement applies to the opening takbīr, Qur’an recitation, tashahhud, and khuṭbah.

f: 247. What is considered in the wording of the adhān regarding languages?
b: The customarily recognized wording of the adhān is considered.

f: 248. Is it valid to begin the prayer by saying "اللهم اغفر لي" (O Allah, forgive me)?
b: No, because it contains a personal request and is not pure glorification of Allah, which is required for the opening of prayer.

f: 249. Is it valid to begin the prayer by saying only "اللهم" (O Allah)?
b: There are two opinions: one says it is valid because it means "Yā Allah"; another says it is not valid because it functions as a request rather than pure glorification.

f: 250. Where should a person place the right hand during standing in prayer according to the Ḥanafī school?
b: The right hand should be placed over the left hand below the navel.

f: 251. What evidence is used for placing the hands below the navel during prayer?
b: The narration: "It is from the Sunnah to place the right hand over the left hand below the navel."

f: 252. Which opinions are contradicted by placing the hands below the navel?
b: It contradicts Mālik’s view of leaving the hands at the sides and al-Shāfiʿī’s view of placing them on the chest.

f: 253. Why is placing the hands below the navel considered more appropriate according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because it is closer to humility and submission, which is the purpose of standing in prayer.

f: 254. Is placing one hand over the other during standing in prayer considered Sunnah according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: Yes, it is Sunnah during standing positions in which there is prescribed remembrance.

f: 255. In which prayer positions is placing the hands over one another recommended according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: During the standing with recitation, the qunūt of witr, and the funeral prayer.

f: 256. In which standing positions should the hands be left at the sides according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: During the standing after rukūʿ and between the takbīrs of the Eid prayers.

f: 257. What supplication is recited after the opening takbīr according to the famous narrations?
b: "Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa biḥamdik..."

f: 258. Did Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله recommend adding the verse "Indeed, I have turned my face..." after the opening supplication?
b: Yes, based on the narration from ʿAlī that the Prophet ﷺ said it.

f: 259. Why did Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad not add "Indeed, I have turned my face..." after the opening supplication?
b: Because of the narration of Anas رضي الله عنه that the Prophet ﷺ began prayer with the takbīr and "Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa biḥamdik" without adding anything else.

f: 260. How did Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad interpret the narration mentioning "Indeed, I have turned my face..."?
b: They interpreted it as referring to voluntary night prayer (tahajjud), not obligatory prayers.

f: 261. Should a person say "wa jalla thanā’uk" (and exalted is Your praise) in the opening supplication of obligatory prayers?
b: No, because it is not mentioned in the well-known narrations.

f: 262. Should the opening supplication be said before or after the opening takbīr?
b: It is better not to say it before the takbīr, so that the intention connects directly with the takbīr.

f: 263. What should a person recite after the opening supplication?
b: They should seek refuge with Allah from Satan by saying "Aʿūdhu billāhi min al-shayṭān al-rajīm."

f: 264. Why is istiʿādhah (seeking refuge) said before Qur’an recitation?
b: Due to Allah’s statement: "When you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed."

f: 265. Is istiʿādhah connected to the opening praise or to Qur’an recitation according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: It is connected to Qur’an recitation, not the opening praise.

f: 266. Should a latecomer (masbūq) say istiʿādhah when joining the prayer?
b: Yes, because it is connected to recitation.

f: 267. Should istiʿādhah be delayed during Eid takbīrs?
b: Yes, according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad, unlike Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله.

f: 268. Should the basmalah be recited before Qur’an recitation in prayer?
b: Yes, it should be recited.

f: 269. Should the basmalah be recited aloud in prayer according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, it should be recited quietly.

f: 270. What evidence do the Ḥanafīs use for saying the basmalah quietly?
b: The statement of Ibn Masʿūd that the imam hides four things, including istiʿādhah, basmalah, and Āmīn.

f: 271. Does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله require saying the basmalah at the beginning of every rakʿah?
b: One narration says he does not require it, like istiʿādhah. Another narration says he does it as a precaution.

f: 272. Should the basmalah be recited between Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and another sūrah?
b: According to Muḥammad, it is recited in prayers where the recitation is silent.

f: 273. What should a person recite after the basmalah in prayer?
b: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah followed by another sūrah or three verses from any sūrah.

f: 274. Is reciting Sūrat al-Fātiḥah considered a pillar (rukn) of prayer according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, it is not considered a pillar, although it is obligatory.

f: 275. Is adding another sūrah after al-Fātiḥah considered a pillar according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, but it is obligatory in the relevant prayers.

f: 276. What evidence do the Ḥanafīs use that any Qur’an recitation is sufficient?
b: Allah’s statement: "Recite whatever is easy of the Qur’an."

f: 277. Why do the Ḥanafīs say reports requiring al-Fātiḥah cannot establish a pillar?
b: Because a solitary report cannot add an additional pillar to what is established by the Qur’an, although it can establish an obligation.

f: 278. What should the imam and follower say when the imam finishes al-Fātiḥah and says "wa lā al-ḍāllīn"?
b: Both should say "Āmīn."

f: 279. What evidence supports saying Āmīn after the imam?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When the imam says Āmīn, then say Āmīn."

f: 280. Should Āmīn be said aloud according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: No, it should be said quietly.

f: 281. Why is Āmīn said quietly according to the Ḥanafīs?
b: Because it is a supplication, and supplication is generally performed quietly.

f: 282. Is elongating Āmīn recommended?
b: There are two opinions regarding elongation, but exaggerating the emphasis in it is a serious mistake.

f: 283. How should the takbīr when moving into rukūʿ be performed?
b: It should be said while descending into rukūʿ.

f: 284. Should the takbīrs in prayer be prolonged?
b: No, they should be said briefly.

f: 285. Why should the beginning of "Allāhu Akbar" not be prolonged?
b: Because it changes it into a question form.

f: 286. Why should the end of "Akbar" not be incorrectly extended?
b: Because it becomes a grammatical mistake in Arabic.

f: 287. How should the hands be placed during rukūʿ?
b: The hands should rest on the knees with the fingers spread apart.

f: 288. Why are the fingers spread during rukūʿ?
b: Because it allows a stronger grip on the knees.

f: 289. Should the fingers be spread in all prayer positions?
b: No, spreading is specifically recommended in rukūʿ and joining is recommended in sujūd.

f: 290. How should the back be positioned during rukūʿ?
b: The back should be made straight and level.

f: 291. Should the head be raised or lowered during rukūʿ?
b: No, the head should neither be raised nor lowered excessively.

f: 292. What should be said in rukūʿ?
b: "Subḥāna rabbiyal-ʿaẓīm" three times.

f: 293. What does "three times is the minimum" mean regarding rukūʿ glorification?
b: It means three repetitions represent the minimum level of completeness.

f: 294. What does the imam say when rising from rukūʿ?
b: "Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah."

f: 295. What does the follower say after rising from rukūʿ?
b: "Rabbana laka al-ḥamd."

f: 296. Does the imam say "Rabbana laka al-ḥamd" according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله the imam only says the tasmiʿ ("Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah").

f: 297. Do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say the imam should also say "Rabbana laka al-ḥamd"?
b: Yes, they say he should say it quietly.

f: 298. What evidence does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله use for restricting the imam to tasmiʿ?
b: The Prophet’s ﷺ statement: "When the imam says Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah, then say Rabbana laka al-ḥamd," which assigns each phrase to a different person.

f: 299. Should a person praying alone say both "Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah" and "Rabbana laka al-ḥamd"?
b: Yes, this is the more correct opinion.

f: 300. What is the ruling on rising fully upright after the first prostration and sitting between the two prostrations according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad رحمهما الله, standing fully upright after the first prostration and sitting between the two prostrations are not obligatory pillars of the prayer.

f: 301. What is the ruling on the sitting between the two prostrations and standing upright after the first prostration according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and al-Shāfiʿī?
b: According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and al-Shāfiʿī رحمهما الله, both are obligatory, based on the ḥadīth: “Stand and pray, for you have not prayed.”

f: 302. What is the reasoning of Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad for not making the sitting and standing between prostrations obligatory?
b: They argue that rukūʿ linguistically means bending and sujūd means lowering oneself, so the minimum action fulfilling these meanings is sufficient for the pillars. The transitions are not themselves intended acts of worship.

f: 303. What did Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad consider the ruling of the sitting and standing between prostrations?
b: They considered them sunnah acts.

f: 304. What was the view of al-Karkhī regarding tranquility (ṭumaʾnīnah) in rukūʿ and sujūd?
b: Al-Karkhī رحمه الله considered tranquility in rukūʿ and sujūd obligatory, such that leaving it forgetfully requires the prostrations of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw).

f: 305. How should a person place his hands when going into prostration?
b: He should place his hands on the ground, as this was described from the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ.

f: 306. Where should a person place his face and hands during prostration according to the narration mentioned?
b: He should place his face between his hands, with his hands positioned parallel to his ears.

f: 307. What parts of the face should a person prostrate upon according to the preferred practice?
b: He should prostrate upon both his nose and forehead, as the Prophet ﷺ consistently did.

f: 308. Is it valid to prostrate only on the forehead according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, prostrating on only one part of the face is valid.

f: 309. What is the position of Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad regarding prostrating only on the nose?
b: They held that prostrating only on the nose is not valid unless there is an excuse.

f: 310. What evidence did Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad use for requiring the forehead in prostration?
b: They used the ḥadīth that the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to prostrate on seven bones, including the forehead.

f: 311. What is Abū Ḥanīfah’s رحمه الله response regarding prostration on only part of the face?
b: He argued that prostration is fulfilled by placing part of the face, since the command mentions the face generally.

f: 312. Are placing the hands and knees on the ground obligatory in prostration according to the Hanafi school?
b: No, placing the hands and knees is sunnah according to the Hanafi school.

f: 313. What did al-Qudūrī mention regarding placing the feet during prostration?
b: Al-Qudūrī رحمه الله mentioned that placing the feet is obligatory in prostration.

f: 314. Is prostrating on the fold of a turban or extra part of clothing valid?
b: Yes, it is valid to prostrate on the fold of a turban or the extra part of one's garment.

f: 315. What evidence is mentioned for the permissibility of prostrating on clothing?
b: It is mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ sometimes prostrated on the fold of his turban and prayed in a single garment, protecting himself from the heat and cold of the ground.

f: 316. What is recommended regarding exposing the arms during prostration?
b: It is recommended to expose the arms and not keep them pressed against the body.

f: 317. Why should a person keep his arms away from his sides during prostration?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ would keep his arms away from his sides during prostration.

f: 318. Should a person keep his arms spread out when praying in a congregation?
b: If he is in a row, he should not spread them in a way that harms the person beside him.

f: 319. How should a person position his stomach in relation to his thighs during prostration?
b: He should keep his stomach away from his thighs during prostration.

f: 320. How should the toes be positioned during prostration?
b: The toes should face the qiblah.

f: 321. What should a person say in prostration?
b: He should say: “Subḥāna Rabbiy al-Aʿlā” three times.

f: 322. What is the minimum level of completeness regarding saying “Subḥāna Rabbiy al-Aʿlā” in prostration?
b: Saying it three times is the minimum level of complete glorification.

f: 323. Is it recommended to increase the number of tasbīḥs in rukūʿ and sujūd?
b: Yes, it is recommended to increase them beyond three, provided one ends with an odd number.

f: 324. How much should an imam increase the tasbīḥ in rukūʿ and sujūd?
b: An imam should not increase it to the extent that it burdens or annoys the congregation.

f: 325. What is the ruling of the tasbīḥ of rukūʿ and sujūd in the prayer?
b: The tasbīḥ of rukūʿ and sujūd is sunnah.

f: 326. How should a woman perform prostration according to the Hanafi school?
b: A woman lowers herself closely and presses her stomach against her thighs because this is more concealing for her.

f: 327. What should a person do after the first prostration?
b: He raises his head, says the takbīr, and sits.

f: 328. What is the ruling if a person does not sit fully between the two prostrations and immediately performs the second prostration?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Muḥammad رحمهما الله, it is valid if he raises enough that he is closer to sitting than prostrating.

f: 329. What is the criterion for whether the brief sitting between prostrations counts?
b: If the person is closer to prostration, it does not count; if he is closer to sitting, it counts.

f: 330. How should a person rise after the second prostration?
b: He should rise standing on the fronts of his feet without sitting or using his hands on the ground.

f: 331. What is the Shāfiʿī position regarding rising after the second prostration?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī رحمه الله held that a person should perform a brief sitting before standing and may use his hands for support.

f: 332. How does the Hanafi school respond to the Shāfiʿī evidence about sitting before standing?
b: They interpret those reports as applying to a person who is elderly or has difficulty standing.

f: 333. What should a person do in the second rakʿah compared to the first rakʿah?
b: He performs the same actions as in the first rakʿah.

f: 334. What actions are not repeated in the second rakʿah?
b: The opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ) and seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) are not repeated.

f: 335. Does a person raise his hands for takbīrs after the opening takbīr according to the Hanafi school?
b: No, he only raises his hands for the initial takbīr.

f: 336. What is the Shāfiʿī position regarding raising the hands during rukūʿ and rising from rukūʿ?
b: Al-Shāfiʿī رحمه الله held that the hands should also be raised during these movements.

f: 337. How should a person sit after completing the second prostration of the second rakʿah?
b: He sits by placing his left foot under him, sitting on it, and keeping the right foot upright with the toes facing the qiblah.

f: 338. What evidence is mentioned for the Hanafi sitting posture in prayer?
b: The description of the Prophet’s ﷺ sitting in prayer from ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها is mentioned.

f: 339. Where should the hands be placed while sitting for tashahhud?
b: The hands should be placed on the thighs with the fingers extended.

f: 340. How should a woman sit during tashahhud according to the Hanafi school?
b: She sits on her left hip and extends both feet to the right side because this is more concealing for her.

f: 341. What wording of the tashahhud is recited according to al-Hidāyah?
b: The tashahhud is: “Al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, wa al-ṣalawātu wa al-ṭayyibāt, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabī…” until the end. This is the tashahhud of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه.

f: 342. Why is the tashahhud of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه preferred over the tashahhud of Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما?
b: Because Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught him this tashahhud directly, just as he taught him a sūrah from the Qur’an.

f: 343. What is the difference between the tashahhud of Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنهما?
b: Ibn Masʿūd’s wording begins “al-Taḥiyyātu lillāh…” while Ibn ʿAbbās’s wording includes “al-taḥiyyātu al-mubārakātu…” and “salāmun ʿalaynā wa ʿalā ʿibādillāh al-ṣāliḥīn.”

f: 344. Why is the wording of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه preferred according to al-Hidāyah?
b: Because it contains the command of the Prophet ﷺ (“say: al-taḥiyyātu…”), and the additions in other narrations are treated as extra wording rather than the original teaching.

f: 345. What is the ruling on adding extra words to the first tashahhud?
b: One should not add beyond the prescribed tashahhud in the first sitting.

f: 346. Why does one not make supplication after the first tashahhud?
b: Because Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught the tashahhud for both the middle and final sitting: in the middle sitting he would stand after finishing the tashahhud, while in the final sitting he would supplicate.

f: 347. What is recited in the last two rakʿahs of a four-rakʿah prayer?
b: Only Sūrat al-Fātiḥah is recited in the last two rakʿahs.

f: 348. Is reciting al-Fātiḥah in the last two rakʿahs obligatory or recommended according to al-Hidāyah?
b: It is the preferred method; the obligation of recitation in the last two rakʿahs is discussed separately.

f: 349. How does the worshipper sit in the final sitting of prayer?
b: He sits in the same manner as he sat in the first sitting.

f: 350. Why does al-Hidāyah prefer the sitting style of the first sitting over tawarruk?
b: Because it is more difficult on the body, and therefore more suitable for prayer. The narration of the Prophet ﷺ sitting in tawarruk is considered weak or interpreted as applying to old age.

f: 351. What is the ruling of the final tashahhud according to the Hanafis?
b: The final tashahhud is wājib (obligatory).

f: 352. Is sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ in the final sitting a pillar of prayer according to the Hanafis?
b: No. According to the Hanafis it is not a farḍ, unlike the view of al-Shāfiʿī رحمه الله.

f: 353. What evidence do the Hanafis use that ṣalāh upon the Prophet ﷺ is not a farḍ in prayer?
b: They cite the hadith: “When you have said this or done this, your prayer is complete; if you wish, stand, and if you wish, sit.”

f: 354. What is the ruling of sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ outside of prayer according to the scholars mentioned?
b: It is obligatory either once in a person’s lifetime according to al-Karkhī, or every time the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned according to al-Ṭaḥāwī.

f: 355. What type of supplication may be made after the final tashahhud?
b: One may supplicate with words resembling Qur’ānic expressions or established prophetic supplications.

f: 356. What evidence is given for allowing personal supplication after tashahhud?
b: The Prophet ﷺ told Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه: “Then choose from supplications whatever is most pleasing and beloved to you.”

f: 357. Why should a person begin his supplication by praising and sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Because it is more likely to lead to acceptance of the supplication.

f: 358. What type of supplication is not allowed during prayer?
b: Supplications resembling ordinary human speech should not be made, as they may invalidate the prayer.

f: 359. Why should a person avoid saying supplications that resemble normal speech?
b: Because prayer requires expressions appropriate to worship, so established supplications are preferred.

f: 360. Is it valid to say “O Allah, marry me” as a supplication in prayer?
b: It is disliked/avoided because it resembles ordinary speech between people.

f: 361. Is it valid to say “O Allah, forgive me” during prayer?
b: Yes, because this is something only Allah can do and it does not resemble human speech.

f: 362. Is saying “O Allah, provide for me” considered similar to human speech?
b: The correct view mentioned is that it resembles human speech because people also use the term “provide” for one another.

f: 363. How does a person end the prayer according to al-Hidāyah?
b: He gives salām to his right saying: “Al-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatullāh,” then gives salām to his left with the same wording.

f: 364. What evidence is given for turning the head during salām?
b: Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه reported that the Prophet ﷺ would give salām to his right until the whiteness of his right cheek could be seen, and similarly on the left.

f: 365. Whom does a person intend with the first salām?
b: He intends the people praying on his right, men and women, and the recording angels.

f: 366. Whom does a person intend with the second salām?
b: He intends those on his left, men and women, and the recording angels.

f: 367. Should a person intend women in the salām according to the practice of later times?
