f: 775. Why should he pray the Sunnah of Fajr before joining in this situation?
b: Because he can combine both virtues: the Sunnah of Fajr and joining the congregation.

f: 776. If someone fears missing both rakʿahs of Fajr with the imam, what should he do?
b: He should join the imam immediately.

f: 777. Why should someone join the imam instead of praying the Sunnah Fajr when he may miss the whole prayer?
b: Because the reward of congregation is greater and the warning against missing it is stronger.

f: 778. Why is the ruling different for the Sunnah before Ẓuhr?
b: Because it can be performed after the obligatory prayer within its time.

f: 779. What does performing the Sunnah Fajr at the mosque door indicate?
b: It indicates that praying it inside the mosque while the imam is already praying is disliked.

f: 780. What is the general preferred place for voluntary and Sunnah prayers?
b: The home is generally preferred, based on what is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ.

f: 781. If someone misses the two rakʿahs of Fajr Sunnah, can he pray them before sunrise?
b: No, because they would become an unrestricted voluntary prayer, which is disliked after Fajr.

f: 782. Can the missed Sunnah of Fajr be made up after sunrise according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: No.

f: 783. What is the view of Muḥammad regarding making up the missed Sunnah of Fajr?
b: He preferred that it be made up until midday.

f: 784. What evidence did Muḥammad use for making up the Sunnah of Fajr after sunrise?
b: The Prophet ﷺ made them up after sunrise on the morning following the night of al-Taʿrīs when he missed Fajr.

f: 785. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله not allow making up Sunnah prayers after their time?
b: Because the original rule is that Sunnah prayers are not made up; only obligatory prayers require make-up.

f: 786. How do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله explain the hadith about making up Fajr Sunnah?
b: They say it was made up together with the obligatory Fajr prayer, not independently.

f: 787. Until when can the Sunnah of Fajr be made up according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: It can be made up along with Fajr until midday.

f: 788. Are other missed Sunnah prayers made up after their time?
b: No, they are not made up individually after their time.

f: 789. If someone catches only one rakʿah of Ẓuhr with the imam, has he attained the congregational prayer according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, he has not prayed Ẓuhr as a congregational prayer.

f: 790. What is Muḥammad’s view regarding someone who catches only one rakʿah of Ẓuhr?
b: He says he has attained the virtue of congregation.

f: 791. Why does Muḥammad say someone who catches the end of the prayer attains the virtue of congregation?
b: Because whoever reaches the end of something is considered to have reached it.

f: 792. Does catching only one rakʿah make someone truly considered to have prayed Ẓuhr in congregation?
b: No, he gains the reward but did not perform the prayer in congregation in reality.

f: 793. If someone swears “I will not catch the congregation,” does catching one rakʿah break his oath?
b: Yes, according to the distinction mentioned.

f: 794. If someone swears “I will not pray Ẓuhr in congregation,” does catching one rakʿah break his oath?
b: No, because he did not actually pray the whole prayer in congregation.

f: 795. If someone enters a mosque where the obligatory prayer has already finished, may he pray voluntary prayers before the obligatory prayer time ends?
b: Yes, he may pray as much as he wishes if there is sufficient time.

f: 796. What condition applies to praying voluntary prayers after missing the congregation?
b: There must be enough time remaining.

f: 797. Does this allowance include the Sunnah of Fajr and the Sunnah before Ẓuhr?
b: Some scholars exclude them due to their special importance.

f: 798. What evidence shows the special importance of the Sunnah of Fajr?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Pray them even if horses drive you away.”

f: 799. What evidence shows the special importance of the four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever leaves the four before Ẓuhr will not receive my intercession.”

f: 800. What is the preferred approach regarding missed Sunnah prayers when there is enough time?
b: It is better not to abandon them because they complete the obligatory prayers.

f: 801. When may someone leave these Sunnahs despite their virtue?
b: When fearing that the prayer time will expire.

f: 802. If someone reaches the imam while he is in rukūʿ, says the takbīr, and remains standing until the imam rises, has he caught that rakʿah?
b: No, he has not caught that rakʿah.

f: 803. What is Zufar’s view regarding someone who reaches the imam in rukūʿ but does not bow with him?
b: He considers him to have caught the rakʿah.

f: 804. Why does Zufar consider him to have caught the rakʿah?
b: Because he joined the imam in a state that has the ruling of standing.

f: 805. What is the Hanafi response to Zufar’s position?
b: The condition is sharing in the actual actions of prayer, and he did not share in either standing or rukūʿ.

f: 806. If a follower bows before the imam and the imam catches up with him while he is in rukūʿ, is his rakʿah valid?
b: Yes, it is valid.

f: 807. What is Zufar’s view regarding a follower who bows before the imam?
b: He says it is not valid because the action before the imam is not counted.

f: 808. Why do the Hanafis consider it valid when the imam catches him in rukūʿ?
b: Because the condition is only that they share in one part of the prayer, which occurs when the imam joins him in rukūʿ.

f: 809. What should a person do if he misses a prayer and later remembers it?
b: He must make it up (qaḍāʾ) when he remembers it and perform it before the current obligatory prayer.

f: 810. What is the ruling of the order between missed prayers and the current prayer according to the Hanafis?
b: Maintaining order between missed prayers and the current prayer is required.

f: 811. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s view regarding the order between missed prayers and the current prayer?
b: He considers it recommended, not a condition.

f: 812. What evidence do the Hanafis use for requiring order between missed prayers and the current prayer?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, and only remembers it while he is with the imam, let him pray the prayer he is currently in, then pray the one he remembered, then repeat the one he prayed with the imam.”

f: 813. When does the obligation of maintaining order between missed prayers and the current prayer fall?
b: When the time for the current prayer is becoming too narrow, when one forgets the missed prayers, or when there are many missed prayers.

f: 814. Why does order fall when the current prayer time is becoming narrow?
b: Because preserving the current prayer from leaving its time takes precedence.

f: 815. If someone fears missing the current prayer time, what should he do first?
b: He should pray the current prayer first and then make up the missed prayer.

f: 816. If someone prayed the current prayer first while fearing the time would end, is it valid?
b: Yes, because the prohibition against delaying order no longer applies due to the excuse.

f: 817. If someone intentionally prays the current prayer before a missed prayer while there is enough time, is it valid?
b: No, because he performed it before fulfilling the required order.

f: 818. How should multiple missed prayers be arranged when making them up?
b: They should be arranged in the same order in which they were originally obligated.

f: 819. What evidence supports arranging missed prayers in their original order?
b: The Prophet ﷺ missed four prayers during the Battle of the Trench and made them up in order, then said: “Pray as you have seen me praying.”

f: 820. When does order between missed prayers no longer apply?
b: When the missed prayers exceed six prayers.

f: 821. Why does order fall when the missed prayers become numerous?
b: Because the number of missed prayers becomes excessive and maintaining order becomes difficult.

f: 822. What is the threshold for “many missed prayers” according to the Hanafis?
b: Six missed prayers, meaning when the time of the sixth missed prayer has passed.

f: 823. What is meant by the statement: “If he missed more than a day and night, the prayer he begins with is sufficient”?
b: Once missed prayers exceed one day and night, the requirement of order falls.

f: 824. What is Muhammad’s view regarding when order falls among missed prayers?
b: He considers it to fall when the time of the sixth prayer enters.

f: 825. If old and recent missed prayers are combined, may someone pray the current prayer while remembering recent missed prayers?
b: There is disagreement: some permit it due to the large number of missed prayers, while others do not as a disciplinary measure.

f: 826. If someone makes up some missed prayers until only a few remain, does order return?
b: According to some scholars, yes; this is the stronger position.

f: 827. What narration from Muhammad supports the return of order when only a few missed prayers remain?
b: The case of someone who missed one day and night of prayers and began making them up alongside each current prayer.

f: 828. What happens if someone prays ʿAṣr while remembering that he has not prayed Ẓuhr?
b: His ʿAṣr prayer is invalid, unless he is in the final part of the prayer time.

f: 829. What issue does praying ʿAṣr before missed Ẓuhr relate to?
b: The issue of maintaining order between missed prayers and current prayers.

f: 830. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, what happens if the obligatory status of a prayer becomes invalid due to lack of order?
b: The original prayer remains valid, but its description of being obligatory is removed.

f: 831. According to Muḥammad, what happens if the obligatory status is removed?
b: The prayer itself becomes invalid because the opening takbīr was made for an obligatory prayer.

f: 832. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله say the prayer remains valid?
b: Because the opening takbīr was for the essence of prayer with the attribute of obligation, so losing the attribute does not necessarily remove the أصل (foundation).

f: 833. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, what is the status of the ʿAṣr prayer performed before making up Ẓuhr?
b: Its invalidity is suspended.

f: 834. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, when does that suspended invalidity disappear?
b: If the person completes six prayers without repeating Ẓuhr, the prayers become valid.

f: 835. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad, what is the status of that ʿAṣr prayer?
b: It is permanently invalid and can never become valid.

f: 836. If someone prays Fajr while remembering that he has not prayed Witr, what is the ruling according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: His Fajr prayer is invalid.

f: 837. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله say Fajr becomes invalid if Witr was missed?
b: Because Witr is obligatory according to him.

f: 838. What is the view of Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad regarding Witr?
b: They consider it Sunnah, not obligatory.

f: 839. Is there an order between obligatory prayers and Sunnah prayers?
b: No, there is no required order between them.

f: 840. If someone prayed ʿIshāʾ without wuḍūʾ, then prayed the Sunnah and Witr, and later discovered the mistake, what must he repeat according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: He repeats ʿIshāʾ and its Sunnah, but not Witr.

f: 841. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله not require repeating Witr in this case?
b: Because Witr is an independent obligation according to him.

f: 842. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad, what must he repeat in this case?
b: He must repeat Witr as well because it follows ʿIshāʾ.

f: 843. When is سجود السهو (prostration of forgetfulness) required?
b: It is required due to additions or omissions in the prayer.

f: 844. When is سجود السهو performed according to the Hanafis?
b: After the salām, followed by tashahhud and another salām.

f: 845. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s view regarding the timing of سجود السهو?
b: He prefers it before the salām.

f: 846. What evidence do the Hanafis use for performing سجود السهو after salām?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “For every forgetfulness there are two prostrations after the salām.”

f: 847. Why do the Hanafis place سجود السهو after salām?
b: Because reports about the Prophet’s ﷺ actions before and after salām conflict, so his explicit statement is preferred.

f: 848. Why is سجود السهو delayed until after salām?
b: Because it does not repeat, so it is suitable to place it after completing the prayer.

f: 849. If someone forgets the salām itself, can سجود السهو correct it?
b: Yes, because it can compensate for such forgetfulness.

f: 850. How many salāms are given after سجود السهو according to the preferred Hanafi view?
b: Two salāms.

f: 851. Should one send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ and make duʿāʾ after the tashahhud of سجود السهو?
b: Yes, according to the preferred view, because duʿāʾ belongs at the end of prayer.

f: 852. Why is سجود السهو considered obligatory according to the Hanafis?
b: Because it repairs a deficiency that occurs in an act of worship, similar to the compensatory sacrifice in Ḥajj.

f: 853. What is the general principle for when سجود السهو becomes necessary?
b: It becomes necessary when a person leaves an obligatory action, delays it, or delays a pillar unintentionally.

f: 854. Why does adding something extra to the prayer require سجود السهو?
b: Because an addition necessarily involves delaying a pillar or leaving an obligation.

f: 855. When is سجود السهو required due to leaving an action?
b: It is required when a person leaves an action that is described as Sunnah, meaning an obligation established through the Sunnah.

f: 856. What does the author mean by calling some actions “Sunnah” while requiring سجود السهو for leaving them?
b: He means their obligation is established through prophetic practice rather than through the Qur’an.

f: 857. Is leaving the recitation of al-Fātiḥah in prayer a cause for سجود السهو?
b: Yes, because reciting al-Fātiḥah is obligatory.

f: 858. Is leaving the Qunūt of Witr a cause for سجود السهو?
b: Yes, because Qunūt is one of the obligatory actions.

f: 859. Is leaving the tashahhud a cause for سجود السهو?
b: Yes, because tashahhud is obligatory.

f: 860. Which tashahhud does the ruling include?
b: It includes both the first and final tashahhud, as well as the recitation of the tashahhud words.

f: 861. Why are the takbīrs of the two Eid prayers considered obligations?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ consistently performed them and did not abandon them, which indicates obligation.

f: 862. Why do these actions being connected to the whole prayer indicate obligation?
b: Because they are among the special characteristics of the prayer, and such characteristics are established as obligations.

f: 863. If the imam recites loudly where recitation should be silent, is سجود السهو required?
b: Yes.

f: 864. If the imam recites silently where recitation should be loud, is سجود السهو required?
b: Yes.

f: 865. Why is سجود السهو required when the imam changes loud and silent recitation?
b: Because loud recitation in its place and silent recitation in its place are obligatory aspects of prayer.

f: 866. What amount of loudness or silence requires سجود السهو?
b: The amount by which the prayer would be valid if it were done that way.

f: 867. Why does a small amount of loudness or silence not require سجود السهو?
b: Because it cannot be avoided, while a large amount can be avoided.

f: 868. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, what amount of loud recitation is considered significant?
b: One verse.

f: 869. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad, what amount is considered significant?
b: Three verses.

f: 870. Does the ruling of loud and silent recitation apply to a person praying alone?
b: No, because loudness and silence in this context are specific to congregational prayer.

f: 871. Does the imam’s forgetfulness require the followers to perform سجود السهو?
b: Yes, because the reason requiring it exists in the one being followed.

f: 872. Why must the follower perform سجود السهو when the imam does?
b: Because the follower’s prayer is connected to the imam’s prayer.

f: 873. If the imam does not perform سجود السهو, should the follower perform it alone?
b: No, because he would be opposing his imam.

f: 874. If the follower forgets something in prayer, does the imam or the follower perform سجود السهو?
b: No one performs it because the follower cannot do it independently from the imam.

f: 875. If the follower performed سجود السهو alone after his own mistake, what would happen?
b: He would be contradicting his imam.

f: 876. If someone forgets the first sitting and remembers while closer to sitting than standing, what should he do?
b: He should return to sitting and perform the tashahhud.

f: 877. Why does someone who is closer to sitting return to sit?
b: Because what is close to something takes its ruling.

f: 878. Does someone who returns to the first sitting after nearly standing perform سجود السهو?
b: The stronger view is that he does not.

f: 879. If someone remembers the first sitting only when he is closer to standing, should he return?
b: No, because he is treated like someone standing.

f: 880. What must someone do if he leaves the first sitting and does not return because he is closer to standing?
b: He performs سجود السهو because he left an obligatory action.

f: 881. If someone forgets the final sitting and stands for a fifth rakʿah, when can he return?
b: He may return as long as he has not performed the prostration of the fifth rakʿah.

f: 882. Why may he return before prostrating the fifth rakʿah?
b: Because correcting the prayer is still possible, and less than a complete rakʿah can be rejected.

f: 883. What happens to the fifth rakʿah when he returns to the final sitting?
b: It is cancelled.

f: 884. Does he perform سجود السهو after returning from the fifth rakʿah?
b: Yes, because he delayed an obligatory action.

f: 885. What happens if he completes the fifth rakʿah by performing its prostration?
b: His obligatory prayer becomes invalid according to the Hanafis.

f: 886. Why does completing the fifth rakʿah invalidate the obligatory prayer?
b: Because he has firmly begun a voluntary prayer before completing the obligatory prayer.

f: 887. What does the fifth rakʿah become according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: The prayer becomes voluntary (nafl).

f: 888. What does Muḥammad say regarding this case?
b: He disagrees according to the previously mentioned principle.

f: 889. After the prayer becomes voluntary, what should the person do?
b: He should add a sixth rakʿah.

f: 890. If he does not add a sixth rakʿah, is there any sin upon him?
b: No, because the matter is based on a juristic assumption.

f: 891. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, when does the fifth rakʿah become established?
b: When the forehead is placed in prostration.

f: 892. According to Muḥammad, when does the fifth rakʿah become established?
b: When the person raises his head from prostration because completion occurs with the final action.

f: 893. Where does the difference between Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad appear?
b: In cases such as someone experiencing a nullifier during the fifth rakʿah prostration.

f: 894. If someone sits in the fourth rakʿah, then stands without giving salām, what should he do?
b: He should return to sitting as long as he has not prostrated for the fifth rakʿah.

f: 895. Why can he return after standing from the fourth rakʿah?
b: Because giving salām while standing is not legislated and the correction is still possible.

f: 896. If he performs the prostration of the fifth rakʿah after this, what should he do?
b: He adds another rakʿah and completes his obligatory prayer.

f: 897. Why does he add another rakʿah after completing the fifth?
b: To make the two extra rakʿahs into a valid voluntary pair, because one isolated rakʿah is not valid as a voluntary prayer.

f: 898. Do the two added rakʿahs replace the Sunnah of Ẓuhr?
b: No, according to the correct view, because the Sunnah requires a separate intention and opening takbīr.

f: 899. Is سجود السهو performed in this situation?
b: Yes, as a matter of preference.

f: 900. Why is سجود السهو performed when extra rakʿahs are added?
b: Because the obligatory prayer was deficient due to leaving the proper method of exiting it.

f: 901. If someone prays two voluntary rakʿahs, performs سجود السهو, and then wants to add two more rakʿahs, may he continue from where he left off?
b: No, he must begin a new prayer.

f: 902. Why can he not build upon the previous voluntary prayer after سجود السهو?
b: Because the سجود السهو occurred in the middle of the prayer and interrupts it.

f: 903. If a traveller performs سجود السهو then intends residence, may he continue his prayer?
b: Yes, because otherwise the entire prayer would become invalid.

f: 904. If someone gives salām while owing سجود السهو and another person joins him afterward, is the newcomer considered part of the prayer?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, only if the imam performs سجود السهو.

f: 905. According to Muḥammad, is the person who joins after salām considered a follower?
b: Yes, whether the imam performs سجود السهو or not.

f: 906. Why does Muḥammad consider the imam still in prayer after salām requiring سجود السهو?
b: Because the salām does not remove him from prayer until the deficiency is repaired.

f: 907. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله consider the salām effective?
b: Because salām normally ends prayer, but its effect is suspended due to the need for سجود السهو.

f: 908. If someone gives salām intending to end the prayer while he still owes سجود السهو, what must he do?
b: He must perform سجود السهو.

f: 909. Why does that salām not end the prayer?
b: Because it was not the legislated salām and his intention to change the proper procedure is ignored.

f: 910. What should someone do if he doubts whether he prayed three or four rakʿahs and this is the first time it happens?
b: He restarts the prayer.

f: 911. What evidence supports restarting the prayer when doubt occurs for the first time?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Let him repeat the prayer.”

f: 912. What should someone do if doubts frequently occur for him?
b: He acts according to what he thinks is most likely correct.

f: 913. What evidence supports following the stronger assumption?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Let him seek what is correct.”

f: 914. What should someone do if he has no dominant opinion when he doubts?
b: He builds upon certainty, which is the lesser number.

f: 915. What evidence supports building upon certainty?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If he does not know whether he prayed three or four, let him build upon the lesser.”

f: 916. Why is ending with salām preferred when building upon certainty?
b: Because salām is a recognized completion of prayer, unlike merely intending to end it.

f: 917. When building upon the lesser number, what should a person do at each possible ending point?
b: He should sit whenever he reaches a point where his prayer could have ended, so he does not leave an obligatory sitting.

f: 918. What should a sick person do if he is unable to stand in prayer?
b: He prays sitting, performing rukūʿ and sujūd normally.

f: 919. What evidence is used for allowing the sick person to pray sitting?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn رضي الله عنه: “Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side making gestures.”

f: 920. What principle determines the obligations of a sick person in prayer?
b: Acts of obedience are according to one’s ability.

f: 921. If a sick person cannot perform rukūʿ and sujūd, how does he pray?
b: He makes gestures (īmāʾ) while sitting.

f: 922. How should the sick person differentiate between his sujūd and rukūʿ when making gestures?
b: He makes the gesture for sujūd lower than the gesture for rukūʿ.

f: 923. Why should sujūd be lower than rukūʿ when gesturing?
b: Because the gestures replace rukūʿ and sujūd and therefore take their rulings.

f: 924. Should a sick person raise something to his face to prostrate on when he cannot reach the ground?
b: No, he should not.

f: 925. What evidence is given against prostrating on something raised to the face?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If you are able to prostrate on the ground, then prostrate; otherwise gesture with your head.”

f: 926. If someone places something on his forehead while lowering his head, is his prayer valid?
b: No, because the required gesture does not occur.

f: 927. If someone lowers his head while the object is present and he does not place his forehead on it, is his prayer valid?
b: Yes, because the gesture exists.

f: 928. If a sick person cannot sit, how should he pray?
b: He lies on his back with his feet facing the qiblah and gestures for rukūʿ and sujūd.

f: 929. What evidence supports praying while lying on the back?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “If he cannot, then on his back making gestures.”

f: 930. Is it valid for a sick person to lie on his side facing the qiblah and gesture?
b: Yes.

f: 931. Which position is preferred: lying on the back or on the side?
b: According to the Hanafis, lying on the back is preferred.

f: 932. Why do the Hanafis prefer lying on the back?
b: Because the gesture of the person on his back points toward the direction of the Kaʿbah, while the person on his side points toward the direction of his feet.

f: 933. If a person cannot even gesture with his head, what happens to the prayer?
b: The prayer is delayed until he becomes able to perform it.

f: 934. Can a person who cannot move his head gesture with his eyes, heart, or eyebrows?
b: No, according to the Hanafis.

f: 935. Why do the Hanafis reject gestures with the eyes or heart?
b: Because establishing substitutes for acts of worship based on personal reasoning is not allowed.

f: 936. Why is head movement different from eye movement?
b: Because the head can fulfill an actual pillar of prayer, while the eyes and similar movements cannot.

f: 937. Does prayer fall from a conscious person who remains unable to gesture for more than a day and night?
b: No, prayer does not fall from him as long as he remains conscious.

f: 938. Why does prayer not fall from a conscious person even after prolonged inability?
b: Because he still understands the obligation addressed to him.

f: 939. Does the same ruling apply to an unconscious person?
b: No, because he does not understand the command.

f: 940. If someone can stand but cannot perform rukūʿ and sujūd, must he stand?
b: No, he may pray sitting while making gestures.

f: 941. Why is standing not required when rukūʿ and sujūd cannot follow it?
b: Because the purpose of standing is to lead into sujūd, which contains the ultimate humility; without sujūd it is not considered a pillar.

f: 942. What is the preferred way for someone who cannot perform rukūʿ and sujūd but can sit?
b: To pray sitting with gestures, because it resembles sujūd more closely.

f: 943. If a healthy person begins praying standing and then becomes sick during the prayer, what does he do?
b: He completes the prayer sitting, performing rukūʿ and sujūd if able, or gestures if unable.

f: 944. If he cannot sit after becoming sick during prayer, what should he do?
b: He prays lying down.

f: 945. Why may he continue from where he stopped after becoming sick?
b: Because he built the lesser state upon the greater state, similar to following an imam.

f: 946. If someone prayed sitting due to illness and then becomes healthy during the prayer, may he continue standing?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, yes.

f: 947. What is Muḥammad’s view if a person praying sitting due to illness becomes healthy?
b: He must restart the prayer.

f: 948. What issue is this disagreement based upon?
b: Their disagreement regarding building upon one state of prayer when moving from a weaker condition to a stronger one.

f: 949. If someone prayed part of his prayer with gestures and then becomes able to perform rukūʿ and sujūd, what does he do?
b: He restarts the entire prayer according to all three imams.

f: 950. Why must he restart after moving from gestures to normal rukūʿ and sujūd?
b: Because the person performing rukūʿ cannot build upon the prayer of the person making gestures.

f: 951. If someone begins a voluntary prayer standing and becomes tired, may he lean on a stick or wall?
b: Yes, if there is a valid excuse.

f: 952. Is leaning without an excuse disliked?
b: Yes, according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad.

f: 953. What is Abū Ḥanīfah’s رحمه الله view regarding leaning without an excuse?
b: It is not disliked according to him.

f: 954. If someone sits during a voluntary prayer without an excuse, is it disliked?
b: Yes, according to all scholars.

f: 955. Is a voluntary prayer performed sitting without excuse valid?
b: According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله it is valid; according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad it is not valid.

f: 956. If someone prays sitting in a ship without an excuse, is his prayer valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, but standing is better.

f: 957. What is the view of Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad regarding praying sitting in a ship?
b: It is not valid unless there is an excuse.

f: 958. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله allow sitting in a ship?
b: Because dizziness and instability are normally present in ships, making the excuse effectively present.

f: 959. Why is standing still preferred in a ship according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: To avoid the doubt of disagreement and because standing is more complete.

f: 960. Is leaving the ship to pray outside better if possible?
b: Yes, because it brings more tranquility to the heart.

f: 961. If someone becomes unconscious for five prayers or fewer, must he make them up?
b: Yes.

f: 962. If someone is unconscious for more than five prayers, must he make them up?
b: No.

f: 963. What is the basis for the ruling that long unconsciousness does not require making up prayers?
b: It is based on juristic preference (istiḥsān).

f: 964. What would the analogy (qiyās) suggest regarding unconsciousness?
b: That no prayers need to be made up if the unconsciousness covers an entire prayer time, because the person was incapable.

f: 965. Why does istiḥsān distinguish between short and long unconsciousness?
b: Because many missed prayers create hardship, while a small number does not.

f: 966. What is considered “long” unconsciousness according to the Hanafis?
b: More than one day and one night.

f: 967. Why is more than one day and one night considered long?
b: Because it enters the level of repetition and abundance.

f: 968. Is unconsciousness compared to insanity in this ruling?
b: Yes, unconsciousness is treated like insanity according to Abū Sulaymān.

f: 969. Why is sleep different from unconsciousness regarding missed prayers?
b: Because prolonged sleep is rare, so it is treated like a short interruption.

f: 970. According to Muḥammad, how is the length of unconsciousness measured?
b: By the number of prayer times missed.

f: 971. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله, how is the length of unconsciousness measured?
b: By hours, based on reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما.

f: 972. How many سجدة التلاوة (prostrations of recitation) are there in the Qur’an according to the Hanafi school?
b: There are fourteen سجدة التلاوة.

f: 973. Which places in the Qur’an contain the fourteen سجدة التلاوة?
b: They are in: the end of Sūrah al-Aʿrāf, al-Raʿd, al-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl (al-Isrāʾ), Maryam, the first سجدة in al-Ḥajj, al-Furqān, al-Naml, Alif Lām Mīm Tanzīl (al-Sajdah), Ṣād, Ḥā Mīm al-Sajdah (Fuṣṣilat), al-Najm, Idhā al-Samāʾ Inshaqqat (al-Inshiqāq), and Iqraʾ (al-ʿAlaq).

f: 974. What is the source for identifying these fourteen places?
b: They are written in the muṣḥaf of ʿUthmān رضي الله عنه, which is the relied-upon source.

f: 975. Which سجدة in Sūrah al-Ḥajj is considered the one for prostration according to the Hanafis?
b: The first سجدة in Sūrah al-Ḥajj.

f: 976. Where is the سجدة in Sūrah Fuṣṣilat (Ḥā Mīm al-Sajdah) according to the view of ʿUmar رضي الله عنه?
b: At the verse: {لَا يَسْأَمُونَ} (Fuṣṣilat: 38).

f: 977. Why is the position of the سجدة in Fuṣṣilat taken at {لَا يَسْأَمُونَ}?
b: Because it is the safer position adopted as a precaution.

f: 978. Is سجدة التلاوة obligatory for the one reciting and the one listening?
b: Yes, it is obligatory for both the reciter and listener.

f: 979. Does سجدة التلاوة become obligatory if someone listens unintentionally?
b: Yes, because it is not restricted by intention.

f: 980. What evidence establishes the obligation of سجدة التلاوة?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The سجدة is upon the one who hears it and the one who recites it.”

f: 981. If the imam recites an ayah of سجدة التلاوة, what should he do?
b: He performs the prostration.

f: 982. What should the followers do when the imam performs سجدة التلاوة?
b: They perform it with him because they are required to follow him.

f: 983. If the follower recites an ayah of سجدة التلاوة during prayer, should the imam perform it?
b: No.

f: 984. Should the follower perform that سجدة during the prayer after reciting it?
b: No.

f: 985. Should the follower perform that سجدة after finishing the prayer?
b: No, according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله.

f: 986. What is Muḥammad’s view regarding a follower who recites an ayah of سجدة during prayer?
b: He says they perform it after finishing the prayer because the cause for it exists and there is no longer an obstacle.

f: 987. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله not require the follower to perform the سجدة after prayer?
b: Because the follower is prevented from reciting independently due to the imam’s authority over his prayer, so the follower’s recitation has no legal effect.

f: 988. Why is the case of a follower different from a person in janābah or menstruation?
b: Because the follower’s recitation has no legal effect due to following the imam, while the others are prohibited from reciting themselves.

f: 989. If a person outside prayer hears an ayah of سجدة from someone praying, must he perform سجدة التلاوة?
b: Yes, according to the correct view.

f: 990. If people in prayer hear an ayah of سجدة from someone outside their prayer, should they perform it during prayer?
b: No.

f: 991. Why should they not perform سجدة التلاوة during prayer when hearing it from someone outside the prayer?
b: Because this hearing is not part of the acts of their prayer.

f: 992. When should they perform that سجدة?
b: After finishing their prayer.

f: 993. If they perform that سجدة during prayer, does it count?
b: No, because it is incomplete due to the prohibition.

f: 994. If they perform سجدة التلاوة during prayer incorrectly, what must they do?
b: They repeat the سجدة after the prayer.

f: 995. Does performing an incorrect سجدة التلاوة invalidate the prayer?
b: No, according to the main view, because the prostration itself does not contradict the state of prayer.

f: 996. What is mentioned in some narrations regarding performing سجدة التلاوة during prayer incorrectly?
b: That the prayer becomes invalid because they added something not belonging to it; this is reported as a view of Muḥammad.

f: 997. If the imam recites an ayah of سجدة and performs it, then someone joins the prayer afterward, must the latecomer perform that سجدة?
b: No, if he joined after the imam already performed it.

f: 998. Why does the latecomer not need to perform it if he joins after the imam’s سجدة?
b: Because by joining the rakʿah he becomes included in it.

f: 999. If someone joins the imam before the imam performs the سجدة, what should he do?
b: He performs the سجدة with the imam.

f: 1000. If someone hears the ayah but does not join the imam, what should he do?
b: He performs the سجدة alone because the cause exists.

f: 1001. If a سجدة التلاوة became obligatory during prayer but was not performed, can it be made up outside prayer?
b: No.

f: 1002. Why is a missed سجدة التلاوة from prayer not made up afterward?
b: Because it is connected specifically to prayer and cannot be fulfilled outside it.

f: 1003. If someone recites an ayah of سجدة, does not perform it, enters prayer, recites the same ayah again, and performs سجدة, does it count for both recitations?
b: Yes, the single سجدة suffices for both.

f: 1004. Why does the second سجدة count for both recitations?
b: Because the second one is stronger since it occurred within prayer.

f: 1005. What is mentioned in the Nawādir regarding this case?
b: That he performs another سجدة after finishing prayer because the first cause occurred earlier.

f: 1006. If someone recites an ayah of سجدة, performs the سجدة, then enters prayer and recites it again, what does he do?
b: He performs another سجدة for the second recitation.

f: 1007. Why does the second recitation require another سجدة in this case?
b: Because the second cause cannot be attached to the first, as that would make the ruling precede its cause.

f: 1008. If someone repeats the same سجدة verse many times in one sitting, how many سجdahs are required?
b: Only one سجدة is sufficient.

f: 1009. If someone recites the سجدة verse, performs the سجدة, leaves and returns to the same place, and recites it again, what happens?
b: He performs another سجدة.

f: 1010. If someone repeats the verse in the same sitting but did not perform the first سجدة, how many سجdahs are required?
b: Two سجdahs are required.

f: 1011. What is the principle behind multiple recitations of the same سجدة verse?
b: The ruling is based on merging the causes to avoid hardship.

f: 1012. Does this merging occur in the cause or the ruling?
b: It occurs in the cause, not the ruling.

f: 1013. Why does the same sitting allow multiple recitations to merge into one سجدة?
b: Because the sitting combines separate actions into one unit.

f: 1014. If the sitting changes, what happens to the obligation?
b: The original rule returns and each recitation requires its own سجدة.

f: 1015. If only the listener changes place while the reciter remains, does the listener’s obligation repeat?
b: Yes, because the cause for him is hearing.

f: 1016. If only the reciter changes place while the listener remains, does the listener’s obligation repeat?
b: According to one view, yes.

f: 1017. What is the more correct view regarding the listener when only the reciter changes place?
b: The obligation does not repeat.

f: 1018. How does a person perform سجدة التلاوة?
b: He says takbīr without raising his hands, prostrates, then says takbīr and raises his head.

f: 1019. Why does سجدة التلاوة not include raising the hands?
b: Because it follows the method of the prostration in prayer.

f: 1020. Is there a tashahhud after سجدة التلاوة?
b: No.

f: 1021. Is there a salām after سجدة التلاوة?
b: No.

f: 1022. Why is there no tashahhud or salām after سجدة التلاوة?
b: Because they are acts of exiting prayer, and سجدة التلاوة has no opening takbīr establishing a prayer state.

f: 1023. Is it disliked to recite a whole sūrah while intentionally skipping the سجدة verse?
b: Yes.

f: 1024. Why is skipping the سجدة verse disliked?
b: Because it resembles turning away from it and refusing to perform it.

f: 1025. Is it permissible to recite only the سجدة verse and leave the rest of the sūrah?
b: Yes.

f: 1026. Why is reciting the سجدة verse alone allowed?
b: Because it is hastening toward fulfilling the سجدة.

f: 1027. What did Muḥammad recommend when reciting only the سجدة verse?
b: He preferred reciting one or two verses before it to avoid the impression that the verse itself is being specially elevated.

f: 1028. What did the scholars recommend regarding reciting سجدة verses aloud?
b: They recommended keeping them hidden (quiet) out of consideration for listeners.

f: 1029. What type of journey is considered travel that changes legal rulings according to the Hanafi school?
b: A journey in which a person intends to travel the distance of three days and nights at the normal pace of camels or walking.

f: 1030. What evidence does al-Hidāyah mention for defining travel as three days and nights?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The resident wipes for a complete day and night, while the traveller wipes for three days and nights.”

f: 1031. Why does the hadith about wiping the khuff indicate a general measurement for travel?
b: Because the concession applies to the general category of travellers, which requires a general estimate.

f: 1032. What was Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله estimate for the distance of travel?
b: Two days and more than half of the third day.

f: 1033. What was one view of al-Shāfiʿī regarding the distance that makes a person a traveller?
b: One day and one night.

f: 1034. How does al-Hidāyah respond to the opinion that travel is only one day and one night?
b: The Sunnah is sufficient evidence against that opinion.

f: 1035. What pace of travel is intended by the phrase “the mentioned walking”?
b: The average pace, not the fastest or slowest pace.

f: 1036. What method of estimating travel distance is reported from Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Measuring by stages (marāḥil), which is close to the three-day estimate.

f: 1037. Are farsakhs (parasangs) used as a reliable measurement for determining travel according to the Hanafi school?
b: No, the correct view is that farsakhs are not considered.

f: 1038. Is travel by sea measured according to the same distance as travel by land?
b: No, the distance of sea travel is not measured according to land travel.

f: 1039. How is the distance of sea travel determined according to the Hanafi school?
b: It is determined according to what is suitable for its circumstances, similar to travelling through mountains.

f: 1040. What is the obligatory prayer length for a traveller performing a four-rakʿah prayer according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Two rakʿahs, and the traveller does not add more than this.

f: 1041. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s view regarding the traveller’s four-rakʿah prayers?
b: The obligation remains four rakʿahs, and shortening is only a concession.

f: 1042. What evidence does the Hanafi school use to show that shortening is obligatory for a traveller?
b: The second two rakʿahs are not made up if missed, and leaving them does not involve sin, which indicates they are voluntary.

f: 1043. Why is shortening prayer different from shortening the fast during travel?
b: The missed fast must be made up later, whereas the extra two rakʿahs of prayer are not made up.

f: 1044. What is the ruling if a traveller prays four rakʿahs and sits for tashahhud after the second rakʿah?
b: The first two rakʿahs count as the obligatory prayer and the last two count as voluntary prayer, although he has acted improperly by delaying the salām.

f: 1045. Why does a traveller who sits after the second rakʿah and completes four rakʿahs become sinful according to the Hanafi school?
b: Because he delayed the salām after completing the obligatory prayer.

f: 1046. What is the ruling if a traveller prays four rakʿahs without sitting for tashahhud after the second rakʿah?
b: The prayer is invalid because the voluntary prayer became mixed with the obligatory prayer before its completion.

f: 1047. When does a traveller begin shortening prayers after leaving his city?
b: When he passes beyond the houses of the city.

f: 1048. Why does leaving the city mark the beginning of travel according to the Hanafi school?
b: Residence is connected to entering the city, so travel is connected to leaving it.

f: 1049. What report from ʿAlī رضي الله عنه is mentioned regarding leaving the city limits?
b: He said that if they passed beyond a certain boundary, they would shorten the prayer.

f: 1050. How long must a traveller intend to stay in a town or village before becoming a resident?
b: Fifteen days or more.

f: 1051. What does a traveller do if he intends to stay less than fifteen days in a town or village?
b: He continues shortening his prayers.

f: 1052. Why did the Hanafi scholars estimate residence as fifteen days?
b: Because travel can include remaining in a place temporarily, so a fixed period was needed, and it was compared to the period of purity (ṭuhr).

f: 1053. Which Companions are mentioned as narrating the fifteen-day period of residence?
b: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما.

f: 1054. Does intending to stay in a wilderness or desert make a traveller a resident?
b: The apparent view is that it does not.

f: 1055. If a traveller enters a city intending to leave tomorrow or the day after tomorrow but remains there for years, does he shorten prayers?
b: Yes, because he never intended a period of residence.

f: 1056. What evidence is mentioned that a person may remain a traveller despite staying for months?
b: Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما stayed in Azerbaijan for six months while shortening prayers.

f: 1057. If an army enters enemy territory and intends to remain there, do they shorten prayers?
b: Yes, they continue shortening prayers.

f: 1058. Why does an army in enemy territory not become resident even if they intend to stay?
b: Because they may either be defeated and remain or be forced to flee, so the place is not considered a stable residence.

f: 1059. If an army besieges a city or fortress in enemy territory, do they shorten prayers?
b: Yes, they shorten prayers.

f: 1060. If an army besieges rebels in Muslim territory outside a city, do they shorten prayers according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, they shorten prayers.

f: 1061. If an army besieges rebels at sea, do they shorten prayers according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, they shorten prayers.

f: 1062. Why does besieging rebels prevent an army from becoming residents?
b: Their uncertain situation prevents a firm intention of settlement.

f: 1063. What is Zufar’s opinion regarding an army that has dominance while besieging enemies?
b: They become residents because they have the apparent ability to settle.

f: 1064. What is Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله opinion regarding an army living in houses of a settled area?
b: They become residents because they are in a place of residence.

f: 1065. What is the ruling regarding nomadic people living in tents and pastures (ahl al-kilāʾ)?
b: The correct view is that they are considered residents.

f: 1066. Why are nomadic people considered residents despite moving between pastures?
b: Residence is their original state and is not cancelled by moving from one pasture to another.

f: 1067. What is the ruling if a traveller follows a resident imam during the prayer time?
b: The traveller completes four rakʿahs.

f: 1068. Why does a traveller praying behind a resident imam complete four rakʿahs?
b: His obligation changes to four because he follows the resident imam.

f: 1069. What is the ruling if a traveller follows a resident imam in a missed prayer?
b: It does not make him complete four rakʿahs.

f: 1070. Why does following a resident imam in a missed prayer not change the traveller’s obligation?
b: Because the prayer time, which caused the obligation, has already passed.

f: 1071. What happens when a traveller leads residents and prays only two rakʿahs?
b: The traveller gives salām, and the residents complete the remaining two rakʿahs.

f: 1072. Why do residents complete their prayer after a travelling imam gives salām?
b: They only followed him for the two rakʿahs he was required to pray, similar to a latecomer completing his prayer.

f: 1073. Should residents recite when completing the remaining two rakʿahs after a traveller imam?
b: The preferred Hanafi view is that they do not recite.

f: 1074. Why do residents not recite when completing their prayer after a traveller imam?
b: Their obligation was already fulfilled through the imam’s prayer, unlike a latecomer whose missed portion was not fulfilled.

f: 1075. What is recommended for a traveller imam to say after giving salām to residents?
b: “Complete your prayer, for we are a travelling people.”

f: 1076. Why is the traveller imam recommended to inform residents to complete their prayer?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ said this when he led the people of Makkah while travelling.

f: 1077. If a traveller enters his own city, does he pray the full prayer even without intending residence?
b: Yes, he completes the full prayer.

f: 1078. Why does entering one’s own city make a traveller a resident without a new intention?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions would return to their homes and become residents without renewing their intention.

f: 1079. If a person leaves his original homeland and permanently settles elsewhere, then returns to his first homeland, does he shorten prayers?
b: Yes, because the first homeland is no longer considered his residence.

f: 1080. What example from the Prophet ﷺ is mentioned regarding returning to a former homeland?
b: After the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ considered himself a traveller in Makkah.

f: 1081. What cancels an original homeland (waṭan aṣlī)?
b: Another original homeland replaces it.

f: 1082. What cancels a residence homeland (waṭan iqāmah)?
b: Another residence homeland, travel, or an original homeland.

f: 1083. If a traveller intends to stay fifteen days in both Makkah and Minā, does he pray the full prayer?
b: No, he continues shortening.

f: 1084. Why does intending residence in both Makkah and Minā not make a traveller a resident?
b: Because considering multiple places as residence would create an impossible situation where travel would never end.

f: 1085. When does a traveller become resident between Makkah and Minā according to the Hanafi school?
b: When he intends to spend the night in one of them.

f: 1086. Why is spending the night relevant for residence between Makkah and Minā?
b: Because a person’s residence is connected to the place where he stays overnight.

f: 1087. If a person misses a prayer while travelling and makes it up while resident, how many rakʿahs does he pray?
b: He makes it up as two rakʿahs.

f: 1088. If a person misses a prayer while resident and makes it up while travelling, how many rakʿahs does he pray?
b: He makes it up as four rakʿahs.

f: 1089. Why is the missed prayer performed according to the original travel or residence status?
b: Because the ruling is based on the state at the end of the prayer time when the obligation became fixed.

f: 1090. Are sinful travellers entitled to travel concessions such as shortening prayers according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, sinful and obedient travellers receive the same concessions.

f: 1091. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s view regarding concessions for sinful travel?
b: A person travelling for sin does not receive travel concessions.

f: 1092. What is the Hanafi response to the view that sinful travellers cannot shorten prayers?
b: The texts granting concessions are general, and travel itself is not sinful; the sin is the action connected to the travel.

f: 1093. Where is the Friday prayer (Jumuʿah) valid according to the Hanafi school?
b: It is only valid in a major city (miṣr jāmiʿ) or in the designated prayer area of the city, and it is not valid in villages.

f: 1094. What evidence is mentioned that Jumuʿah is not held in villages?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “There is no Friday prayer, Eid prayer, or prayer of sacrifice except in a major city.”

f: 1095. What is considered a “major city” (miṣr jāmiʿ) according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: A place that has a ruler and judge who enforce rulings and establish legal punishments.

f: 1096. What other view is reported regarding what qualifies as a major city?
b: Some scholars said it is only a place where people gather in the largest mosque and that the mosque is too small to contain them.

f: 1097. Which opinion regarding the definition of a major city did al-Karkhī prefer?
b: The opinion that any place with a ruler and judge who enforce rulings is a major city.

f: 1098. Are the rulings of Jumuʿah restricted only to the mosque where it is prayed?
b: No, Jumuʿah may be prayed throughout the courtyards and open areas of the city because they are treated as part of the city.

f: 1099. Is Jumuʿah prayer valid in Minā according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: Yes, if the ruler of the Ḥijāz is present or if the caliph is travelling there.

f: 1100. What is Muḥammad’s opinion regarding Jumuʿah prayer in Minā?
b: Jumuʿah is not valid in Minā because it is considered a village.

f: 1101. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله consider Jumuʿah valid in Minā?
b: Because Minā becomes like a city during the pilgrimage season due to the large gathering.

f: 1102. Why is there no repeat Jumuʿah prayer in Minā according to the Hanafi explanation?
b: Because this is a concession to make matters easier for pilgrims.

f: 1103. Is Jumuʿah prayer valid in ʿArafāt according to the Hanafi scholars?
b: No, all three Hanafi imams agree that there is no Jumuʿah in ʿArafāt.

f: 1104. Why is Jumuʿah not valid in ʿArafāt but valid in Minā?
b: ʿArafāt is an open plain, whereas Minā contains buildings.

f: 1105. Why is the condition of having the caliph or governor of the Ḥijāz mentioned for Minā?
b: Because authority belongs to them, while the seasonal pilgrimage leader only manages pilgrimage matters.

f: 1106. Who is allowed to establish the Friday prayer according to the Hanafi school?
b: Only the ruler or someone appointed by the ruler.

f: 1107. Why must Jumuʿah be established by the ruler or his appointed representative?
b: Because it involves a large gathering where disputes over leadership and organization may occur.

f: 1108. What is the time condition for the validity of Jumuʿah prayer?
b: It must be performed during the time of Ẓuhr.

f: 1109. Is Jumuʿah prayer valid after the time of Ẓuhr has ended?
b: No, it is not valid after the time has passed.

f: 1110. What should people do if the time of Jumuʿah ends while they are praying it?
b: They begin the Ẓuhr prayer instead and do not continue building upon the Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1111. Why is Jumuʿah not completed after its time ends?
b: Because Jumuʿah and Ẓuhr are different prayers.

f: 1112. Is the Friday sermon (khuṭbah) a condition for Jumuʿah?
b: Yes, the khuṭbah is one of its conditions.

f: 1113. Why is the Friday sermon considered a condition of Jumuʿah?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ never prayed Jumuʿah without delivering a sermon.

f: 1114. When is the Friday sermon delivered?
b: After the time of Ẓuhr begins and before the prayer.

f: 1115. How many sermons are delivered for Jumuʿah prayer?
b: Two sermons separated by a sitting.

f: 1116. How should the imam deliver the Friday sermon according to the established practice?
b: He should deliver it standing and while in a state of purity.

f: 1117. Why is standing during the Friday sermon recommended?
b: Because it was the established practice transmitted from the early generations.

f: 1118. Is the Friday sermon valid if the imam sits or delivers it without wudūʾ?
b: Yes, it is valid, although it is disliked because it opposes the established practice.

f: 1119. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, what is the minimum content required for the Friday sermon?
b: Any mention of Allah is sufficient, even a simple statement of praise or glorification.

f: 1120. What do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad require for the Friday sermon?
b: They require a longer speech that is recognized as a sermon.

f: 1121. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say a simple mention of Allah is not enough for the sermon?
b: Because a brief glorification is not normally called a sermon.

f: 1122. What evidence does al-Shāfiʿī use to require two proper sermons?
b: The established custom of Muslims and the practice of delivering two sermons.

f: 1123. What incident involving ʿUthmān رضي الله عنه is mentioned regarding the sermon?
b: He began by saying “Al-ḥamdu lillāh,” then became unable to continue, descended, and prayed.

f: 1124. Is having a congregation a condition for Jumuʿah prayer?
b: Yes, because the word Jumuʿah itself indicates gathering.

f: 1125. How many people besides the imam are required for Jumuʿah according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Three people besides the imam.

f: 1126. How many people besides the imam are required according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: Two people besides the imam.

f: 1127. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad consider two people besides the imam sufficient?
b: Because a pair contains the meaning of gathering.

f: 1128. Why does the Hanafi school consider three people besides the imam to be the proper congregation?
b: Because the true plural form in both wording and meaning begins with three.

f: 1129. If people leave before the imam bows and prostrates in Jumuʿah, leaving only women and children, what is the ruling according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: The imam and remaining people pray Ẓuhr instead.

f: 1130. If people leave after the imam has begun Jumuʿah but before completing a full rakʿah, what is the ruling according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: They complete the Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1131. If people leave after the imam completes one rakʿah and one prostration, what is the ruling according to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad?
b: The imam completes the Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1132. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله require the congregation to remain until one complete rakʿah is completed?
b: Because the prayer does not become established until a complete rakʿah is performed.

f: 1133. Why is the continuation of the congregation not required during the sermon?
b: Because the sermon is separate from the prayer.

f: 1134. Do women and children count as the congregation needed for Jumuʿah?
b: No, because Jumuʿah is not established through them.

f: 1135. Who is not obligated to attend Jumuʿah prayer according to the Hanafi school?
b: The traveller, woman, sick person, slave, and blind person.

f: 1136. Why is a traveller excused from attending Jumuʿah?
b: Because attending may cause hardship.

f: 1137. Why is a sick person excused from attending Jumuʿah?
b: Because attending may cause harm or hardship.

f: 1138. Why is a slave excused from attending Jumuʿah?
b: Because he is occupied with serving his master.

f: 1139. Why is a woman excused from attending Jumuʿah?
b: Because she may be occupied with serving her husband.

f: 1140. If a traveller, woman, sick person, slave, or blind person attends Jumuʿah, does it replace their Ẓuhr prayer?
b: Yes, it fulfills the obligation of that time.

f: 1141. Can a traveller, slave, or sick person lead Jumuʿah prayer according to the Hanafi school?
b: Yes, their Jumuʿah is valid if they attend.

f: 1142. Why does Zufar disagree with allowing a traveller, slave, or sick person to lead Jumuʿah?
b: Because they are not originally obligated to perform Jumuʿah, similar to a child or woman.

f: 1143. Why does the Hanafi school allow a traveller, slave, or sick person to lead Jumuʿah?
b: Because when they attend, the obligation applies to them due to their participation.

f: 1144. Can a woman lead men in Jumuʿah prayer according to the Hanafi school?
b: No, because a woman is not suitable to lead men.

f: 1145. If someone prays Ẓuhr at home on Friday before the imam performs Jumuʿah without an excuse, is his prayer valid?
b: Yes, but it is disliked.

f: 1146. Why does the Hanafi school consider praying Ẓuhr before Jumuʿah valid?
b: Because the original obligation for everyone is Ẓuhr, while Jumuʿah is an alternative commanded in place of it.

f: 1147. What is Zufar’s opinion about praying Ẓuhr before Jumuʿah without excuse?
b: He says it is not valid because Jumuʿah is the original obligation and Ẓuhr is only its substitute.

f: 1148. If a person prayed Ẓuhr at home and then decides to attend Jumuʿah while the imam is praying, does his Ẓuhr become invalid according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: Yes, his Ẓuhr becomes invalid simply by going toward Jumuʿah.

f: 1149. According to Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad, when does the earlier Ẓuhr prayer become invalid after deciding to attend Jumuʿah?
b: Only when he actually joins the imam in Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1150. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله consider walking toward Jumuʿah enough to invalidate the earlier Ẓuhr?
b: Because going to Jumuʿah is a special action connected specifically to Jumuʿah, so it takes its ruling.

f: 1151. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad not invalidate Ẓuhr merely by walking toward Jumuʿah?
b: Because walking is less than the prayer itself and does not cancel an already completed prayer.

f: 1152. Does walking toward Jumuʿah after the imam has finished invalidate the earlier Ẓuhr prayer according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, because it is no longer considered walking toward an active Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1153. Is it disliked for excused people to pray Ẓuhr in congregation in a city on Friday?
b: Yes, it is disliked because it weakens the appearance of Jumuʿah, which gathers the congregations of the city.

f: 1154. Why is it disliked for excused people to pray Ẓuhr in congregation on Friday in a city?
b: Because others may follow them and abandon Jumuʿah, since the excused person may appear to be establishing an alternative congregation.

f: 1155. Is it disliked for people living in villages to pray Ẓuhr in congregation on Friday?
b: No, because Jumuʿah is not obligatory upon them.

f: 1156. If a group of excused people pray Ẓuhr together on Friday, is their prayer valid?
b: Yes, because all the conditions of the prayer are fulfilled.

f: 1157. What should a person do if he catches the imam during Jumuʿah prayer?
b: He joins whatever part he catches and completes what he missed.

f: 1158. What evidence is mentioned for the ruling of joining the imam and completing missed portions?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whatever you catch, pray it; whatever you miss, complete it.”

f: 1159. If a person joins the Jumuʿah imam during the final sitting or during the prostration of forgetfulness, what should he do according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله?
b: He completes it as Jumuʿah.

f: 1160. What is Muḥammad’s opinion if someone joins the imam only during the second rakʿah of Jumuʿah?
b: If he catches most of the second rakʿah, he completes it as Jumuʿah; if he catches less, he completes it as Ẓuhr.

f: 1161. Why does Muḥammad consider a latecomer to Jumuʿah partly like one praying Ẓuhr?
b: Because his prayer resembles Jumuʿah in some aspects but resembles Ẓuhr because some conditions of Jumuʿah were missed.

f: 1162. According to Muḥammad, how does someone who missed part of Jumuʿah complete the prayer?
b: He prays four rakʿahs, sits after two rakʿahs, and recites in the final two because they may be considered additional voluntary prayer.

f: 1163. Why do Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله and Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله say that someone who catches the imam late still completes Jumuʿah?
b: Because he is considered to have caught Jumuʿah, and therefore he must have the intention of Jumuʿah, which consists of two rakʿahs.

f: 1164. What should people do when the imam comes out on Friday for the sermon according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: They should stop praying and speaking until the sermon is finished.

f: 1165. What is the opinion of Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad regarding speaking when the imam comes out before beginning the sermon?
b: They allow speaking because the obligation of listening has not yet begun.

f: 1166. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله prohibit speech when the imam comes out for the sermon?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ said: “When the imam comes out, there is no prayer and no speech.”

f: 1167. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله compare speech during the sermon time to prayer?
b: Because speech can naturally continue for a long time, just as prayer can.

f: 1168. When should people stop buying and selling on Friday?
b: After the first call to prayer (adhān) when it is after midday according to the preferred opinion.

f: 1169. What verse is used as evidence for leaving trade before Jumuʿah?
b: Allah says: “Hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade.” (Qurʾān 62:9)

f: 1170. When the imam sits on the pulpit before the sermon, what happens according to established practice?
b: The callers to prayer give the adhān in front of the pulpit.

f: 1171. How many adhāns were there during the Prophet’s ﷺ time for Jumuʿah?
b: There was only the adhān given when the imam sat on the pulpit.

f: 1172. Which adhān is considered the original one connected to the sermon according to some scholars?
b: The adhān given when the imam sits on the pulpit.

f: 1173. What is the stronger Hanafi opinion regarding which adhān makes trade forbidden and requires attending Jumuʿah?
b: The first adhān, if it occurs after midday, because it informs people of the prayer time.

f: 1174. Who is obligated to perform the Eid prayer according to the Hanafi school?
b: Everyone upon whom Jumuʿah prayer is obligatory.

f: 1175. What is the ruling of Eid prayer according to one narration from Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: It is obligatory (wājib).

f: 1176. What evidence is mentioned for the obligation of Eid prayer?
b: The Prophet ﷺ consistently performed it.

f: 1177. What evidence is mentioned by those who classify Eid prayer as a sunnah?
b: The hadith of the Bedouin where the Prophet ﷺ said after mentioning the obligatory prayers: “No, except if you perform voluntary prayers.”

f: 1178. Why is Eid prayer called a sunnah despite being considered obligatory according to the Hanafi school?
b: Because its obligation is established through the Sunnah rather than direct Qurʾānic evidence.

f: 1179. What should a person do on Eid al-Fiṭr before going to the prayer place?
b: He should eat, perform ghusl, use the siwāk, and apply perfume.

f: 1180. Why is eating before Eid al-Fiṭr prayer recommended?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ used to eat before leaving for the prayer place.

f: 1181. Why is ghusl and perfume recommended on Eid?
b: Because Eid is a gathering day, similar to Friday, where cleanliness and good appearance are encouraged.

f: 1182. What type of clothing did the Prophet ﷺ have for Eid according to the narration mentioned?
b: He had a fur or wool garment that he wore on the two Eids.

f: 1183. Why should a person pay Zakāt al-Fiṭr before Eid prayer?
b: So that the poor are provided for and can focus their hearts on the prayer.

f: 1184. Does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله recommend saying takbīr while travelling to the Eid prayer place on Eid al-Fiṭr?
b: No, he does not recommend it.

f: 1185. What do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say regarding takbīr on the way to Eid al-Fiṭr prayer?
b: They recommend it, comparing it to Eid al-Aḍḥā.

f: 1186. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله not recommend takbīr on the way to Eid al-Fiṭr?
b: Because the default in remembrance is concealment, and takbīr was specifically legislated prominently for Eid al-Aḍḥā.

f: 1187. Is voluntary prayer performed before Eid prayer at the prayer place?
b: No, it is disliked because the Prophet ﷺ did not do so.

f: 1188. Does the prohibition of voluntary prayer before Eid apply only in the prayer place?
b: There are two views: some restrict it to the prayer place, while others apply it everywhere.

f: 1189. When does the time for Eid prayer begin?
b: After sunrise has risen sufficiently (when the sun is about the height of a spear).

f: 1190. When does the time for Eid prayer end?
b: When the time of Ẓuhr begins.

f: 1191. What did the Prophet ﷺ do when the moon sighting for Eid was confirmed after midday?
b: He instructed people to go to the prayer place the following day.

f: 1192. How many rakʿahs are in the Eid prayer?
b: Two rakʿahs.

f: 1193. How many extra takbīrs does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله include in the first rakʿah of Eid prayer?
b: Three extra takbīrs after the opening takbīr.

f: 1194. How is the first rakʿah of Eid prayer performed according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: The imam says the opening takbīr, then three additional takbīrs, recites al-Fātiḥah and another sūrah, then says the takbīr for bowing.

f: 1195. How is the second rakʿah of Eid prayer performed according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: The imam begins with recitation, then says three additional takbīrs, followed by the takbīr for bowing.

f: 1196. Whose opinion is the Hanafi method of Eid takbīrs based upon?
b: The opinion of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه.

f: 1197. What is Ibn ʿAbbās رضي الله عنه’s opinion regarding the extra takbīrs in Eid prayer?
b: Five extra takbīrs in the first rakʿah and five in the second rakʿah.

f: 1198. What practice became widespread among people regarding Eid takbīrs?
b: The practice based upon Ibn ʿAbbās’s narration became widespread due to the encouragement of the caliphs.

f: 1199. Why does the Hanafi school prefer Ibn Masʿūd’s narration over Ibn ʿAbbās’s narration?
b: Because additional takbīrs and raising the hands differ from the normal practice, so the lesser amount is preferred.

f: 1200. Why are the extra takbīrs connected with the opening takbīr in the first rakʿah?
b: Because the opening takbīr has greater strength due to being obligatory and occurring first.

f: 1201. Why are the extra takbīrs connected with the bowing takbīr in the second rakʿah?
b: Because there is no opening takbīr in that rakʿah, so they are connected to the only remaining takbīr, the bowing takbīr.

f: 1202. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s position regarding Eid takbīrs?
b: He follows Ibn ʿAbbās’s narration but considers all the extra takbīrs, making the total fifteen or sixteen.

f: 1203. Does the imam raise his hands during the extra takbīrs of the Eid prayer?
b: Yes, according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, he raises his hands during the Eid takbīrs other than the takbīr for bowing.

f: 1204. What evidence is used for raising the hands during Eid takbīrs?
b: The hadith: “Hands are not raised except in seven places,” and Eid takbīrs are included among them.

f: 1205. What is Abū Yūsuf’s رحمه الله opinion regarding raising the hands during Eid takbīrs?
b: Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله says that the hands are not raised during the Eid takbīrs.

f: 1206. What happens after the Eid prayer is completed?
b: The imam delivers two sermons after the prayer.

f: 1207. What is the evidence for giving two Eid sermons after the prayer?
b: This practice has been transmitted through widespread reports.

f: 1208. What topic should the imam teach in the Eid al-Fiṭr sermon?
b: He should teach people about Zakāt al-Fiṭr and its rulings.

f: 1209. Why is Zakāt al-Fiṭr mentioned in the Eid al-Fiṭr sermon?
b: Because Eid al-Fiṭr was connected to it and it was legislated for that purpose.

f: 1210. If someone misses the Eid prayer with the imam, does he make it up?
b: No, he does not make it up.

f: 1211. Why is the Eid prayer not made up individually after missing it?
b: Because this specific form of prayer is only known as an act of worship with its conditions, and those conditions cannot be fulfilled by an individual alone.

f: 1212. If the new moon was obscured and witnesses testify after midday that Eid was seen, when is the Eid prayer performed?
b: It is performed the next day.

f: 1213. Why can Eid prayer be delayed until the next day when the moon sighting is confirmed late?
b: Because the delay occurred due to a valid excuse, and a narration permits this.

f: 1214. If an excuse prevents Eid prayer from being performed on the second day, is it performed afterward?
b: No, it is not performed afterward.

f: 1215. Why is Eid prayer not performed after the second day if it was missed?
b: Because the original ruling is that it is not made up, except for the specific allowance of delaying it one day due to an excuse.

f: 1216. What is recommended on Eid al-Aḍḥā before leaving for prayer?
b: Performing ghusl and applying perfume.

f: 1217. Should a person eat before Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer?
b: No, he should delay eating until after the prayer.

f: 1218. Why is eating delayed on Eid al-Aḍḥā until after the prayer?
b: Because the Prophet ﷺ did not eat on the Day of Sacrifice until he returned and ate from his sacrifice.

f: 1219. What should a person do while travelling to the Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer place?
b: He should recite the takbīr.

f: 1220. What is the evidence for saying takbīr on the way to Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer?
b: The Prophet ﷺ used to say takbīr while travelling to the prayer place.

f: 1221. How many rakʿahs are prayed for Eid al-Aḍḥā?
b: Two rakʿahs.

f: 1222. What happens after the Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer?
b: The imam gives two sermons.

f: 1223. What should be taught in the Eid al-Aḍḥā sermons?
b: The rulings of sacrifice (uḍḥiyah) and the takbīrs of tashrīq.

f: 1224. Why are sacrifice and takbīrs of tashrīq taught in the Eid al-Aḍḥā sermon?
b: Because they are rulings connected to that time, and the sermon is legislated for teaching.

f: 1225. If an excuse prevents Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer on its day, when may it be performed?
b: It may be performed on the second or third day.

f: 1226. Is delaying Eid al-Aḍḥā prayer without an excuse allowed?
b: No, the person is sinful because it contradicts the transmitted practice.

f: 1227. What is the ruling of the gathering called al-Taʿrīf that some people perform on the Day of ʿArafah outside ʿArafah?
b: It is not considered a valid religious practice.

f: 1228. Why is the gathering called al-Taʿrīf not considered an act of worship?
b: Because standing at ʿArafah is an act of worship restricted to a specific place, like other pilgrimage rituals.

f: 1229. When does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله begin the takbīrs of tashrīq?
b: After the Fajr prayer on the Day of ʿArafah.

f: 1230. When does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله end the takbīrs of tashrīq?
b: After the ʿAṣr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhū al-Ḥijjah).

f: 1231. When do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad end the takbīrs of tashrīq?
b: After the ʿAṣr prayer on the final day of the days of tashrīq.

f: 1232. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad extend the takbīrs of tashrīq until the end of the days of tashrīq?
b: They follow the opinion of ʿAlī رضي الله عنه and choose the larger amount as a precaution in acts of worship.

f: 1233. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله limit the takbīrs of tashrīq to a shorter period?
b: He follows the opinion of Ibn Masʿūd رضي الله عنه and avoids adding extra public takbīr that may resemble an innovation.

f: 1234. What is the wording of the takbīr of tashrīq mentioned in al-Hidāyah?
b: “Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar, lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa-Allāhu akbar, Allāhu akbar, wa-li-Allāhi al-ḥamd.”

f: 1235. Who is this wording of the takbīr of tashrīq attributed to?
b: It is transmitted from Ibrāhīm (Khalīl) عليه السلام.

f: 1236. For whom are the takbīrs of tashrīq required according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: For residents of cities who pray the obligatory prayers in the recommended congregations.

f: 1237. Are women’s congregations required to recite takbīrs of tashrīq according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, if they are praying without a man present.

f: 1238. Are travellers required to recite takbīrs of tashrīq according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: No, if there is no resident imam with them.

f: 1239. What do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say regarding who must recite takbīrs of tashrīq?
b: They say everyone who performs an obligatory prayer must recite them.

f: 1240. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad require takbīrs of tashrīq from everyone?
b: Because they consider it connected to the obligatory prayer itself.

f: 1241. When does a woman or traveller become required to recite takbīrs of tashrīq according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: When they follow a resident male imam, because they follow him.

f: 1242. If the imam forgets the takbīr of tashrīq, should the follower also leave it?
b: No, the follower still performs it.

f: 1243. Why does the follower still perform the takbīr if the imam forgets it?
b: Because it is not part of the prayer’s essential actions and the imam’s leadership does not require following him in it.

f: 1244. What is the ruling of the solar eclipse prayer (ṣalāt al-kusūf)?
b: The imam leads the people in two rakʿahs similar to a voluntary prayer.

f: 1245. How many bowings (rukūʿs) are there in each rakʿah of the solar eclipse prayer according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: One bowing in each rakʿah.

f: 1246. What is al-Shāfiʿī’s opinion regarding the solar eclipse prayer?
b: He says there are two bowings in each rakʿah.

f: 1247. What evidence does al-Shāfiʿī use for two bowings in the eclipse prayer?
b: The narration of ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها.

f: 1248. What evidence does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله use for one bowing in the eclipse prayer?
b: The narration of Ibn ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما.

f: 1249. Why is Ibn ʿUmar’s رضي الله عنهما narration preferred according to the Hanafi argument?
b: Because the eclipse was more visible to the men around the Prophet ﷺ, making their observation stronger.

f: 1250. Should the recitation in the solar eclipse prayer be long?
b: Yes, lengthening the recitation is recommended.

f: 1251. Should the recitation in the solar eclipse prayer be silent or aloud according to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله?
b: It should be silent.

f: 1252. What do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say regarding recitation in the solar eclipse prayer?
b: They say it should be aloud.

f: 1253. Why do Abū Yūsuf رحمه الله and Muḥammad say the eclipse prayer is recited aloud?
b: They rely on the narration of ʿĀʾishah رضي الله عنها that the Prophet ﷺ recited aloud.

f: 1254. What narrations does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله use for silent recitation in the eclipse prayer?
b: The narrations of Ibn ʿAbbās and Samurah ibn Jundub رضي الله عنهما.

f: 1255. Why does Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله prefer silent recitation in the eclipse prayer?
b: Because it is a daytime prayer and daytime prayers are generally silent.

f: 1256. What should the imam do after the eclipse prayer?
b: He should make supplication until the sun becomes clear again.

f: 1257. What is the evidence for making supplication during an eclipse?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When you see something frightening, turn to Allah with supplication.”

f: 1258. What is the Sunnah regarding supplications after the eclipse prayer?
b: They should be delayed until after the prayer.

f: 1259. Who should lead the eclipse prayer?
b: The same imam who leads Jumuʿah prayer.

f: 1260. What should people do if the imam is absent for the eclipse prayer?
b: They pray individually.

f: 1261. Why is the eclipse prayer prayed individually if the imam is absent?
b: To avoid disputes and disorder.

f: 1262. Is there a congregational prayer for a lunar eclipse according to the Hanafi school?
b: No, there is no congregation for the lunar eclipse.

f: 1263. How is the lunar eclipse prayer performed according to the Hanafi school?
b: Each person prays individually.

f: 1264. What evidence is given for praying individually during a lunar eclipse?
b: The Prophet ﷺ said: “When you see any of these signs, hasten to prayer.”

f: 1265. Is there a sermon for the eclipse prayer?
b: No, because no sermon has been transmitted for it.

f: 1266. What is Abū Ḥanīfah’s رحمه الله opinion regarding the prayer of seeking rain (ṣalāt al-istisqāʾ)?
b: Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله says that there is no established Sunnah prayer in congregation for seeking rain.

f: 1267. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, if people pray individually during istisqāʾ, is it valid?
b: Yes, praying individually is permissible.

f: 1268. According to Abū Ḥanīfah رحمه الله, what is the essence of istisqāʾ?
b: Istisqāʾ consists of supplication and seeking forgiveness from Allah.
